iec61850.chapter09.l09.example: For an isolated 33-F01 test, an illustrative sequence uses increasing gaps of 1, 2, 4 and 8 ms before longer intervals. These values explain the mechanism and are not universal relay settings.
iec61850.chapter09.l09.check: Prove the subscriber response to missing frames; counting retransmissions at the publisher alone cannot establish scheme dependability.
iec61850.chapter09.l10.title: GOOSE Subscription and External References
iec61850.chapter09.l10.p01: SCL external references describe how inputs depend on data produced elsewhere. For GOOSE, engineering must identify the publisher, source logical node and data attribute, then bind that input to a receiving application function.
iec61850.chapter09.l10.p02: The standard exchange description and a vendor's internal logic binding are separate parts of the workflow. A valid ExtRef may still be unbound inside the relay application. Conversely, a local input name may exist while pointing at an obsolete publisher revision.
iec61850.chapter09.l10.wf02: Resolve external references and stream identity
iec61850.chapter09.l10.wf03: Bind each received member to the intended internal signal
iec61850.chapter09.l10.example: The receiving bay IED maps the 33-F01 trip member to its designated test logic input. Its communication diagnostic and the internal Boolean transition are both checked.
iec61850.chapter09.l10.check: Confirm the application binding after every import; successful file import is not evidence that subscriber logic changed correctly.
iec61850.chapter09.l11.title: GOOSE-Based Breaker Trip
iec61850.chapter09.l11.p01: GOOSE-based tripping uses a received signal as part of an engineered protection path. The receiving logic must evaluate the correct member, data quality, operating mode and supervision state before driving an authorized output.
iec61850.chapter09.l11.p02: Total clearing time includes protection detection, publisher processing, network transfer, subscriber processing, output operation and breaker mechanics. A fast packet timestamp difference does not measure that complete chain. Independent backup protection and failure behavior follow the protection design.
iec61850.chapter09.l11.wf01: Isolate outputs under the approved test procedure
iec61850.chapter09.l11.wf03: Measure receiving logic, trip output and breaker feedback separately
iec61850.chapter09.l11.example: In a test of the 33-F01 trip path, record publisher operation and receiver output with synchronized test equipment. Confirm the intended breaker only, then test stream loss and invalid quality.
iec61850.chapter09.l11.check: Do not bypass physical isolation merely because a message carries a test or simulation indication; receiving behavior is implementation-dependent.
iec61850.chapter09.l12.title: GOOSE-Based Interlocking
iec61850.chapter09.l12.p01: GOOSE interlocking shares equipment states and permissive information between controllers. The receiving controller combines those inputs with local conditions according to the approved switching philosophy and interlocking matrix.
iec61850.chapter09.l12.p02: An absent, stale or invalid input must not silently become a valid permissive. Interlocks also need meaningful operator diagnostics explaining which condition prevents an action. GOOSE communication is only one part of the safety-related switching function; local hardware constraints may remain necessary.
iec61850.chapter09.l12.wf01: List every remote condition and its owner
iec61850.chapter09.l12.wf03: Test permitted and prohibited combinations against the matrix
iec61850.chapter09.l12.example: Closing a 33 kV bay may depend on a remote earth-switch indication. The example permits closing only when the required verified condition is valid; the actual scheme determines all additional checks.
iec61850.chapter09.l12.check: Never present one generic interlocking Boolean expression as suitable for every substation or bus arrangement.
iec61850.chapter09.l13.title: GOOSE Blocking and Protection Schemes
iec61850.chapter09.l13.p01: Blocking schemes use a received condition to inhibit or coordinate another protection element. Permissive schemes require a positive condition before action. The same communication failure can affect these schemes very differently.
iec61850.chapter09.l13.p02: Define timing margins and failure responses from the protection coordination study. A lost blocking signal may reduce selectivity; a lost permissive signal may delay a required trip. Supervision, backup elements and alarms must be evaluated together, including device mode transitions and startup behavior.
iec61850.chapter09.l13.wf02: Allocate blocking or permissive signals explicitly
iec61850.chapter09.l13.wf03: Test delayed, missing, invalid and unexpected inputs
iec61850.chapter09.l13.example: A downstream feeder fault publishes a blocking condition to an upstream element in the illustrative 33 kV scheme. The approved backup timing remains effective if the communication path fails.
iec61850.chapter09.l13.check: Prove the scheme with actual protection settings and timing requirements; a Boolean logic demonstration alone is insufficient.
iec61850.chapter09.l14.title: GOOSE Communication Across Ethernet Switches
iec61850.chapter09.l14.p01: Switches forward GOOSE according to Ethernet membership, VLAN policy and multicast handling. Port tagging and ingress classification must be consistent from the publisher through every trunk to the subscriber.
iec61850.chapter09.l14.p02: Ordinary IGMP snooping controls IP multicast membership and does not automatically learn conventional Layer-2 GOOSE subscriptions. Use supported static multicast forwarding or another documented industrial switching mechanism. Excessive filtering loses required streams, while indiscriminate flooding wastes bandwidth.
iec61850.chapter09.l14.wf01: Trace the stream port by port
iec61850.chapter09.l14.wf02: Inspect VLAN membership and multicast tables
iec61850.chapter09.l14.wf03: Measure discards and delivery under representative traffic
iec61850.chapter09.l14.example: 33-F01's VLAN 200 stream traverses an uplink that allows VLAN 100 only. The subscriber fails even though MMS remains healthy on station VLAN 100.
iec61850.chapter09.l14.check: After fixing one trunk, check the return maintenance path and all intended subscribers; do not assume the whole topology is now correct.
iec61850.chapter09.l15.title: GOOSE Configuration Using SCL Files
iec61850.chapter09.l15.p01: SCL engineering connects the logical GSEControl and DataSet to Ethernet parameters in the Communication section. The GSE entry identifies the logical device and control-block name, avoiding a separate undocumented address spreadsheet as the only source of truth.
iec61850.chapter09.l15.p02: Publisher and subscriber configurations must derive from the same approved revision. XML schema validity catches structural errors, but semantic validation is still needed for references, member order, types and tool-specific application bindings.
iec61850.chapter09.l15.wf01: Validate the publisher DataSet and GSEControl
iec61850.chapter09.l15.wf03: Resolve subscriber inputs and export device configurations
iec61850.chapter09.l15.example: For the illustrative LD0/gcbTrip, verify the GSE element's ldInst and cbName resolve to the actual publisher control block before comparing APPID and MAC in a packet capture.
iec61850.chapter09.l15.check: Treat an XML excerpt as a teaching fragment; a deployable file needs complete device types, services and vendor-supported context.
iec61850.chapter09.l16.title: Multi-Vendor GOOSE Engineering
iec61850.chapter09.l16.p01: Multi-vendor GOOSE integration depends on compatible data types, edition features, supported services and engineering exchange behavior. Using the same protocol name does not guarantee that every optional feature or application binding is interoperable.
iec61850.chapter09.l16.p02: Collect capability statements and test the exact firmware and tools that will be delivered. Check quality handling, test/simulation behavior, configuration revision response and lost-stream supervision. Vendor tool labels may differ even when the underlying standardized data is equivalent.
iec61850.chapter09.l16.wf02: Map publisher members to receiving types
iec61850.chapter09.l16.wf03: Run a joint functional and negative-test matrix
iec61850.chapter09.l16.example: A Siemens-style publisher and ABB-style subscriber are generic equipment roles here. The project must establish their actual supported member types and binding process from model-specific documentation.
iec61850.chapter09.l16.check: Avoid converting an unsupported type by guessing its bit layout; use a documented compatible signal or revise the engineering design.
iec61850.chapter09.l17.title: Practical Example — 33 kV Feeder Trip
iec61850.chapter09.l17.p01: The practical trip example follows one source signal from 33-F01 through a GOOSE stream to a designated receiving IED. It separates the protection operation, multicast delivery, subscriber logic and output confirmation so failures can be located.
iec61850.chapter09.l17.p02: Use a controlled simulator or isolated relay test arrangement. The subscriber must reject the wrong stream and respond correctly to a valid stream, invalid quality and timeout. Capture evidence at both ends when timing or loss is under investigation.
iec61850.chapter09.l17.wf03: Confirm receiver logic and output, then restore the normal test state
iec61850.chapter09.l17.example: Use the allocated APPID 0x1001 and VLAN 200 consistently throughout the exercise. Record the expected DataSet order before toggling the trip member.
iec61850.chapter09.l17.check: Acceptance requires the intended output behavior and failure response; seeing stNum change in Wireshark is only one observation.
iec61850.chapter09.l18.title: GOOSE Testing Using IED Tools
iec61850.chapter09.l18.p01: IED tools and test sets can monitor or simulate GOOSE streams, but their capabilities vary. A passive monitor reads traffic; an active publisher injects messages and can influence connected subscribers if the test boundary is wrong.
iec61850.chapter09.l18.p02: Define the test network and output isolation before enabling simulation. Confirm how the receiver handles test and simulation indications for its edition and operating mode. Test positive reception and intentional mismatches without assuming one vendor's test mode isolates another vendor's outputs.
iec61850.chapter09.l18.wf01: Record baseline traffic and device modes
iec61850.chapter09.l18.wf03: Verify subscriber diagnostics, logic and isolated output response
iec61850.chapter09.l18.example: For 33-F01 FAT, use a separate test switch and a receiving relay with outputs isolated. Test correct and incorrect ConfRev values and record the diagnostic result.
iec61850.chapter09.l18.check: Remove simulated streams and restore modes before releasing the test boundary; verify that normal publishers regain authority.
iec61850.chapter09.l19.title: GOOSE Packet Analysis in Wireshark
iec61850.chapter09.l19.p01: Wireshark can decode GOOSE identity, counters, lifetime and payload fields. Start with the display filter goose, then narrow to an approved APPID or destination MAC. Preserve the full capture so filtering does not discard evidence of competing streams.
iec61850.chapter09.l19.p02: Illustrative field values must agree: a stable retransmission retains state, while a new state changes the relevant payload and stNum. VLAN tags can be stripped by capture hardware, so absence in the capture is not conclusive proof of untagged transmission.
iec61850.chapter09.l19.wf02: Inspect gocbRef, datSet, confRev and ordered data
iec61850.chapter09.l19.wf03: Compare stNum/sqNum and timeAllowedtoLive across packets
iec61850.chapter09.l19.example: For 33-F01, compare one pre-trip frame and the first post-trip frame. Record both the data transition and its receiving-IED interpretation rather than copying a screenshot alone.
iec61850.chapter09.l19.check: Use the field names supported by the installed Wireshark version; decoder labels can change between releases.
iec61850.chapter09.l20.title: GOOSE Troubleshooting
iec61850.chapter09.l20.p01: GOOSE troubleshooting separates publication, network delivery, subscriber acceptance and application execution. A fault at one stage can produce the same high-level symptom as a fault at another, such as a missing interlock or trip.
iec61850.chapter09.l20.p02: Check the last known good configuration and current live identity before editing anything. Duplicate publishers, wrong VLANs, mismatched ConfRev, reordered members and unbound inputs are distinct causes requiring different corrective actions.
iec61850.chapter09.l20.wf02: Capture at the receiving port and inspect acceptance diagnostics
iec61850.chapter09.l20.wf03: Trace the accepted member into logic and output
iec61850.chapter09.l20.example: If the receiver sees the stream but declares a configuration mismatch, repair the coordinated SCL configuration. If it accepts the member but no output changes, inspect application logic and mode conditions.
iec61850.chapter09.l20.check: Repeat normal, timeout and invalid-data tests after repair and archive the final publisher/subscriber revisions together.
iec61850.chapter10.l01.title: Introduction to Process Bus
iec61850.chapter10.l01.p01: The process bus connects process-level equipment, such as merging units, to protection and control applications using engineered digital communication. Sampled Values transfer current and voltage samples; GOOSE may carry binary information where the project uses it.
iec61850.chapter10.l01.p02: Process bus is an architecture, not simply an Ethernet cable replacing every wire. Auxiliary power, safety circuits, instrument-transformer interfaces and local equipment functions remain part of the design. Its performance depends on acquisition, synchronization, network delivery and receiving algorithms working together.
iec61850.chapter10.l01.wf01: Identify every analogue and binary interface
iec61850.chapter10.l01.wf02: Allocate merging units and receiving IEDs
iec61850.chapter10.l01.wf03: Define timing, availability and supervision requirements
iec61850.chapter10.l01.example: For a 132 kV line bay, a merging unit publishes measured currents and voltages to designated protection IEDs. The protection trip path is engineered separately from the measurement stream.
iec61850.chapter10.l01.check: Document which functions are digital and which remain hardwired; do not label a station fully digital from one SV connection.
iec61850.chapter10.l02.title: Conventional vs Digital Substation Architecture
iec61850.chapter10.l02.p01: Conventional protection commonly carries analogue CT/VT secondary signals to panel-mounted relays. A digital process-bus design digitizes signals near their source or through a merging unit and distributes samples over Ethernet.
iec61850.chapter10.l02.p02: The digital design can reduce long analogue cable runs and allow several subscribers, but introduces dependencies on merging-unit health, time alignment and network delivery. Compare complete lifecycle requirements, including testing and maintenance, instead of assuming fewer wires automatically means less engineering.
iec61850.chapter10.l02.wf01: Draw both signal paths from instrument transformer to relay
iec61850.chapter10.l02.wf02: Compare failure points and test access
iec61850.chapter10.l02.wf03: Select the architecture that satisfies the project performance requirements
iec61850.chapter10.l02.example: The 132 kV line example replaces the measurement link to two protection IEDs with an engineered SV stream. Required independent protection channels must retain the independence specified by the protection philosophy.
iec61850.chapter10.l02.check: Do not accidentally merge Main 1 and Main 2 dependencies into one unprotected merging unit or power supply.
iec61850.chapter10.l03.title: Sampled Values Communication
iec61850.chapter10.l03.p01: Sampled Values transport sequences of instantaneous measurements rather than occasional SCADA magnitudes. Protection algorithms use correctly ordered, scaled and time-related samples to calculate quantities and make decisions.
iec61850.chapter10.l03.p02: An SV stream is continuous traffic with a defined profile, channel arrangement and sample rate. Missing, duplicated or delayed samples can affect the receiving application differently from a delayed MMS measurement. The receiver's documented supervision and fallback behavior must be understood.
iec61850.chapter10.l03.wf02: Agree channel order, scaling and sampling
iec61850.chapter10.l03.wf03: Verify the subscriber's measured quantities against a known injected waveform
iec61850.chapter10.l03.example: Inject a balanced three-phase test current into the 132 kV bay measurement chain. Compare phase magnitude, angle and sequence at the merging unit and each receiving protection IED.
iec61850.chapter10.l03.check: Receiving Ethernet frames alone does not prove correct analogue interpretation; phase order and scaling errors can look like valid communication.
iec61850.chapter10.l04.title: Merging Unit Fundamentals
iec61850.chapter10.l04.p01: A merging unit acquires analogue instrument-transformer signals or supported digital sensor inputs, processes them and publishes synchronized sample information. Its channel count, input ratings, accuracy and output profiles are device-specific.
iec61850.chapter10.l04.p02: The merging unit becomes part of the protection measurement chain. Configuration must cover nominal ratings, channel assignment, timing source and health supervision. A correct network setting cannot compensate for an incorrect analogue ratio or reversed polarity at the input.
iec61850.chapter10.l04.wf01: Match input interfaces to the instrument transformers
iec61850.chapter10.l04.wf03: Test magnitude, polarity, phase angle and health indications
iec61850.chapter10.l04.example: MU_132_L01 supplies the illustrative 132 kV line protection stream. Its current channels correspond to phases A, B and C in the approved wiring schedule, with any neutral channel explicitly identified.
iec61850.chapter10.l04.check: Check the complete measurement-chain accuracy requirements and calibration evidence, including the merging unit and connected sensors.
iec61850.chapter10.l05.title: Current Transformer and Voltage Transformer Inputs
iec61850.chapter10.l05.p01: CT and VT inputs have different electrical behavior and installation requirements. Conventional CT secondary circuits require controlled handling because opening an energized secondary can create dangerous voltage; VT secondary circuits require appropriate protection against short circuits.
iec61850.chapter10.l05.p02: A training diagram shows functional relationships, not terminal instructions for live equipment. Actual polarity, earthing, test links, ratings and protection must follow approved drawings and qualified site procedures. Digital output does not remove these analogue-side obligations.
iec61850.chapter10.l05.wf01: Review approved CT/VT drawings and test boundaries
iec61850.chapter10.l05.wf02: Verify ratios, polarity and channel allocation with suitable equipment
iec61850.chapter10.l05.wf03: Record injected and received quantities before release
iec61850.chapter10.l05.example: For MU_132_L01, phase-A current and voltage channels are verified individually before a three-phase test. A swapped phase is corrected in the approved wiring/configuration record, not hidden by an unexplained display label.
iec61850.chapter10.l05.check: Never disconnect an energized CT secondary to create a test failure; use the approved isolation and shorting arrangement.
iec61850.chapter10.l06.title: Digital and Conventional Instrument Transformers
iec61850.chapter10.l06.p01: Conventional instrument transformers produce analogue secondary quantities. Digital instrument-transformer systems may use different sensing and electronic conversion arrangements, with output interfaces governed by their specified standards and product design.
iec61850.chapter10.l06.p02: Do not assume every optical or low-power sensor can connect to any merging unit. Compatibility includes sensor interface, power, timing, scaling and diagnostic behavior. The protection application needs a traceable relationship between primary quantity and delivered digital sample.
iec61850.chapter10.l06.wf01: Identify the sensor technology and rated interface
iec61850.chapter10.l06.wf02: Match the receiving electronics and profile
iec61850.chapter10.l06.wf03: Test the complete chain at representative operating points
iec61850.chapter10.l06.example: A low-power sensor proposed for the 132 kV bay requires its documented interface module. A conventional 1 A CT input on another merging unit is not a substitute merely because both ultimately publish SV.
iec61850.chapter10.l06.check: Obtain the manufacturer's supported combination and accuracy declaration; protocol compatibility cannot prove analogue interface compatibility.
iec61850.chapter10.l07.title: IEC 61850-9-2 and IEC 61869-9 Overview
iec61850.chapter10.l07.p01: IEC 61850-9-2 defines the Ethernet mapping for sampled values. IEC 61869-9 addresses the digital interface of instrument transformers and associated profiles. Historical 9-2LE implementation guidance is a particular interoperability approach, not a synonym for every 9-2 implementation.
iec61850.chapter10.l07.p02: Profile selection determines details such as sampling, channel arrangement and frame organization. A publisher and subscriber must support the same applicable profile. Never infer compatibility solely from both datasheets mentioning IEC 61850 or process bus.
iec61850.chapter10.l07.wf01: Record exact editions and implemented profiles
iec61850.chapter10.l07.wf03: Validate one representative stream before expanding the design
iec61850.chapter10.l07.example: The line-bay exercise can use an agreed 9-2LE-style profile or a compatible IEC 61869-9 profile. It does not mix their rates and channel conventions in one unexplained configuration.
iec61850.chapter10.l07.check: Use the project-selected profile documents and device manuals for exact numeric settings and limits.
iec61850.chapter10.l08.title: Sampled Value Publisher and Subscriber
iec61850.chapter10.l08.p01: The SV publisher sends measurement streams to subscribing protection or metering devices. Several subscribers may consume one stream, but each must associate the stream with the correct electrical circuit and measurement channels.
iec61850.chapter10.l08.p02: Binding includes stream identification, profile, configuration revision and channel interpretation. A receiver can decode a frame successfully while assigning phase-A current to the wrong protection input. Functional injection testing is therefore essential after communication setup.
iec61850.chapter10.l08.wf01: Allocate the stream and subscriber list
iec61850.chapter10.l08.wf02: Bind channel identities to protection inputs
iec61850.chapter10.l08.wf03: Verify every receiving device with phase-selective injection
iec61850.chapter10.l08.example: MU_132_L01 publishes to Main 1 and Main 2 IEDs only where the protection design permits that shared dependency. Each subscriber is tested independently for the same phase and ratio interpretation.
iec61850.chapter10.l08.check: Record the subscriber application binding, not only the MAC and APPID fields in the network register.
iec61850.chapter10.l09.title: Sampled Value Ethernet Frames
iec61850.chapter10.l09.p01: Conventional SV Ethernet frames use EtherType 0x88BA. Their application content includes stream identification, sample count, configuration information and sample data according to the selected profile and edition.
iec61850.chapter10.l09.p02: APPID and destination MAC identify delivery context, while fields such as svID and smpCnt help interpret the stream. The number of ASDUs per Ethernet frame can vary by profile. Frame rate and sample rate are therefore not always equal.
iec61850.chapter10.l09.wf02: Inspect ASDU count, svID and configuration revision
iec61850.chapter10.l09.wf03: Compare sample counters and channel layout with the selected profile
iec61850.chapter10.l09.example: An illustrative stream carries 4,800 samples per second with two samples per frame only if both endpoints support that specific configuration. Its frame rate is then 2,400 frames per second.
iec61850.chapter10.l09.check: Do not apply that example to a one-ASDU profile or treat the encoded integer sample as primary amperes without scaling.
iec61850.chapter10.l10.title: Sampling Rates and Synchronization
iec61850.chapter10.l10.p01: Sampling rate defines how frequently the analogue waveform is represented. Some profiles describe samples per nominal power-system cycle, while others use fixed samples per second. These conventions must be identified before calculating traffic or comparing devices.
iec61850.chapter10.l10.p02: Synchronization aligns sample timing across sources when the receiving application requires it. A counter progressing smoothly does not prove that two merging units sample the same instant. Accuracy and holdover requirements come from the protection application and profile.
iec61850.chapter10.l10.wf02: Calculate samples and frames per second
iec61850.chapter10.l10.wf03: Test phase alignment and receiver behavior during timing degradation
iec61850.chapter10.l10.example: At 50 Hz, an illustrative 80-samples-per-cycle profile yields 4,000 samples per second. At 60 Hz the corresponding calculation is 4,800; this does not make every SV profile frequency-dependent.
iec61850.chapter10.l10.check: Keep sample rate, frame rate, nominal frequency and synchronization status as separate configuration fields.
iec61850.chapter10.l11.title: Process Bus Ethernet Network Design
iec61850.chapter10.l11.p01: Process-bus networks must carry continuous SV traffic plus engineered GOOSE and timing messages. Capacity planning includes Ethernet overhead, redundancy duplication, multicast distribution and worst-case paths, not just the sample payload size.
iec61850.chapter10.l11.p02: Constrain each stream to intended receivers using supported switch features. Check egress bottlenecks, queue behavior and mirror-port capacity. A network that works with one merging unit can fail after all bays are enabled or after a redundant path failure concentrates traffic.
iec61850.chapter10.l11.wf02: Map aggregate traffic on every link
iec61850.chapter10.l11.wf03: Test normal and degraded paths with the full intended stream set
iec61850.chapter10.l11.example: For the 132 kV bay, calculate the MU stream load from measured frame size and frame rate, then include both PRP networks separately if PRP is selected.
iec61850.chapter10.l11.check: Reserve engineering margin from the project design; do not assert a universal safe utilization percentage for all switches and applications.
iec61850.chapter10.l12.title: Sampled Values and PTP
iec61850.chapter10.l12.p01: PTP can provide the precise timing needed by compatible process-bus equipment. The selected profile defines message behavior and interoperability expectations; IEC/IEEE 61850-9-3 is the power-utility profile used where specified.
iec61850.chapter10.l12.p02: Grandmaster quality, hardware timestamping, switch clock behavior and path asymmetry influence delivered accuracy. Merely receiving PTP packets does not prove synchronized sampling. The receiver must expose suitable timing health and react correctly when the reference is lost or changes.
iec61850.chapter10.l12.wf01: Verify matching PTP profile and domain
iec61850.chapter10.l12.wf02: Inspect master selection and offset diagnostics
iec61850.chapter10.l12.wf03: Test loss, holdover and restoration while observing SV quality and protection behavior
iec61850.chapter10.l12.example: MU_132_L01 obtains time through a compatible PTP network. During a controlled grandmaster interruption, the test records its synchronization indication and the line IED's documented response.
iec61850.chapter10.l12.check: Keep PTP time quality and individual sample quality distinct; one field does not summarize every measurement-chain failure.
iec61850.chapter10.l13.title: Protection IED Subscription to SV
iec61850.chapter10.l13.p01: Protection subscription assigns received SV channels to specific algorithm inputs. Correct communication identity is necessary, but protection also requires the right ratios, polarity, phase sequence, nominal frequency and measurement source allocation.
iec61850.chapter10.l13.p02: Some IEDs support only particular profiles or numbers of streams. Resource and compatibility checks must precede configuration. Subscription supervision should identify absent streams, invalid samples and synchronization problems without silently substituting plausible-looking values.
iec61850.chapter10.l13.wf02: Map every current and voltage channel
iec61850.chapter10.l13.wf03: Perform phase-selective and multi-phase secondary-injection tests
iec61850.chapter10.l13.example: For the 132 kV line IED, inject phase-A current only and confirm the phase-A measurement and intended protection response. Repeat for the remaining phases and voltage channels.
iec61850.chapter10.l13.check: Check protection calculations and operating direction after mapping; a correct RMS magnitude can still conceal a phase-angle or polarity error.
iec61850.chapter10.l14.title: Process Bus Redundancy
iec61850.chapter10.l14.p01: Redundancy protects selected communication failure modes. PRP sends copies across two independent LANs; HSR sends copies along the ring paths. Both require compatible equipment and a design that avoids common failure dependencies.
iec61850.chapter10.l14.p02: Network redundancy does not duplicate the merging unit, its input circuit, auxiliary supply or timing reference automatically. A fully redundant measurement architecture must examine those sources separately. Receiver behavior under duplicates and path changes must be tested with the intended profile.
iec61850.chapter10.l14.wf02: Select and verify the redundancy topology
iec61850.chapter10.l14.wf03: Interrupt each path separately while observing sample continuity and protection health
iec61850.chapter10.l14.example: With PRP, MU_132_L01 and its subscribing IED connect to independent LAN A and LAN B. Disconnecting LAN A should leave a valid path through LAN B within the tested design assumptions.
iec61850.chapter10.l14.check: Do not bridge PRP LAN A and LAN B with an ordinary switch; that defeats their intended separation.
iec61850.chapter10.l15.title: Process Bus Engineering Using SCL
iec61850.chapter10.l15.p01: SCL describes sampled-value control configuration, DataSets, communication addressing and references needed for system engineering. Device tools also establish the internal analogue channel and protection bindings that make the exchange useful.
iec61850.chapter10.l15.p02: Check the supported SCL edition and profile-specific fields before importing. Schema-valid XML can still refer to the wrong merging unit or a channel arrangement unsupported by the receiver. Keep the system configuration and both endpoint exports under revision control.
iec61850.chapter10.l15.wf02: Configure the SV publisher and Communication/SMV entry
iec61850.chapter10.l15.wf03: Resolve subscriptions and verify deployed configuration against the SCD
iec61850.chapter10.l15.example: The illustrative MU_132_L01 stream identity is used consistently in the SCD, receiver configuration and capture evidence. A renamed stream requires coordinated updates, not just a changed drawing.
iec61850.chapter10.l15.check: Validate sample rate, ASDU arrangement, revision and channel mapping together after any SCL round trip.
iec61850.chapter10.l16.title: Sampled Value Quality and Data Validity
iec61850.chapter10.l16.p01: Sample quality indicates whether measurement data should be trusted for its intended use. Relevant indications depend on the profile and implementation and may include invalidity, failure, out-of-range or other conditions. Synchronization is another essential dimension of stream health.
iec61850.chapter10.l16.p02: The receiving protection application needs an engineered policy for degraded inputs. Continuing indefinitely with a frozen last sample is not equivalent to valid measurement. Alarm, blocking, fallback and backup protection behavior must be specified and tested.
iec61850.chapter10.l16.wf01: List supported quality and synchronization indications
iec61850.chapter10.l16.wf02: Define the receiving action for each relevant condition
iec61850.chapter10.l16.wf03: Inject controlled failures and confirm application behavior
iec61850.chapter10.l16.example: During an isolated 132 kV line test, mark the selected channel invalid through supported test equipment and observe the receiver's quality alarm and documented protection response.
iec61850.chapter10.l16.check: Do not invent a universal rule that every bad-quality sample immediately trips or blocks every protection function.
iec61850.chapter10.l17.title: Practical Example — 132 kV Line Protection
iec61850.chapter10.l17.p01: The practical line-bay example includes instrument transformers, MU_132_L01, a process network and subscribing line protection. The test follows measurement information from known injected waveforms to the protection calculation and separately verifies the trip output path.
iec61850.chapter10.l17.p02: Use an agreed channel schedule and profile throughout the exercise. Document the Main 1/Main 2 independence requirement before sharing equipment. Network availability, timing quality and analogue correctness must all be demonstrated rather than inferred from a healthy Ethernet link.
iec61850.chapter10.l17.wf02: Inject normal load and representative fault waveforms
iec61850.chapter10.l17.wf03: Test stream loss, timing degradation and restored operation
iec61850.chapter10.l17.example: Record primary-equivalent current, voltage, phase angle, SV stream identity, receiving measurements and protection operating result for each test. Keep the analogue stimulus and network capture on a common evidence timeline.
iec61850.chapter10.l17.check: Acceptance limits come from the protection study and procurement specification, not from the illustrative diagram.
iec61850.chapter10.l18.title: Process Bus FAT/SAT Testing
iec61850.chapter10.l18.p01: Process-bus FAT proves compatible equipment and engineered behavior before site installation. SAT verifies actual fibre paths, instrument-transformer connections, merging-unit identity, timing distribution and protection interfaces in the installed bay.
iec61850.chapter10.l18.p02: The acceptance plan should distinguish measurement accuracy, communication performance, synchronization and functional protection tests. A packet analyzer cannot certify analogue accuracy, and a correct injection result under normal conditions does not prove failure-mode behavior.
iec61850.chapter10.l18.wf01: Approve test boundaries and acceptance criteria
iec61850.chapter10.l18.wf02: Test every channel and normal operating function
iec61850.chapter10.l18.wf03: Exercise network, time and publisher failures with recorded recovery
iec61850.chapter10.l18.example: For MU_132_L01, include channel polarity, sample profile, subscriber mapping, invalid quality and redundant-path interruption. At site, reconcile every tested channel with the approved as-built terminal schedule.
iec61850.chapter10.l18.check: Use suitable calibrated equipment and authorized isolation procedures; no live CT disturbance is required to demonstrate communication loss.
iec61850.chapter10.l19.title: Sampled Value Packet Analysis
iec61850.chapter10.l19.p01: SV packet analysis identifies stream rate, counter progression, identity and quality information visible at the capture point. Use the sv display filter and inspect fields such as sv.appid, sv.svID and sv.smpCnt supported by the installed decoder.
iec61850.chapter10.l19.p02: Counter discontinuities can arise from capture loss as well as network or publisher problems. Mirror ports can be oversubscribed by multiple high-rate streams. Compare receiver diagnostics and capture statistics before attributing missing frames to the process network.
iec61850.chapter10.l19.wf01: Capture one identified stream at sufficient capacity
iec61850.chapter10.l19.wf02: Check ASDU/sample counter progression and rate
iec61850.chapter10.l19.wf03: Correlate anomalies with receiver logs and injected waveform tests
iec61850.chapter10.l19.example: For MU_132_L01, calculate frames per second separately from samples per second. If two ASDUs are carried per frame, inspect both sample counts rather than assuming one count per packet.
iec61850.chapter10.l19.check: An illustrative decoded-field table is not a genuine measured capture; retain original pcapng files for actual acceptance evidence.
iec61850.chapter10.l20.title: Process Bus Troubleshooting
iec61850.chapter10.l20.p01: Troubleshooting proceeds from the physical measurement chain to the publisher, network, timing system and subscriber application. A wrong phase magnitude with healthy stream counters suggests a different cause from a missing-stream alarm.
iec61850.chapter10.l20.p02: Separate ratio/polarity errors, profile mismatch, multicast filtering, sample loss and clock degradation. Changing several parameters simultaneously can conceal the cause and invalidate previously accepted tests. Restore a controlled baseline before comparing results.
iec61850.chapter10.l20.wf01: Classify the symptom as analogue, communication, timing or application
iec61850.chapter10.l20.wf03: Correct one cause and repeat the relevant functional and failure tests
iec61850.chapter10.l20.example: If the line IED reports swapped phase angles with normal packet delivery, inspect channel mapping and polarity. If counters stop at the receiving port, trace stream delivery before changing protection settings.
iec61850.chapter10.l20.check: Close the issue only after documenting the cause, updated configuration and successful repeat test under the original failing condition.
iec61850.chapter11.l01.title: Introduction to Substation Configuration Language
iec61850.chapter11.l01.p01: Substation Configuration Language (SCL) is the XML-based engineering exchange language defined by IEC 61850-6. It describes relevant system structure, IED information models, communication configuration and relationships between equipment and functions.
iec61850.chapter11.l01.p02: SCL is not a universal executable program for all relay logic. Different file roles carry different engineering information, and vendor tools still manage supported application details. The value of SCL is a controlled, machine-readable exchange between engineering stages.
iec61850.chapter11.l01.wf01: Identify the engineering task and file role
iec61850.chapter11.l01.wf03: Validate structure and references before importing
iec61850.chapter11.l01.example: The 33-F01 relay's model is incorporated into a station configuration so the gateway and GOOSE subscribers use coordinated references instead of independently typed names.
iec61850.chapter11.l01.check: Keep the original vendor export and the approved system revision; successful XML parsing alone does not prove deployability.
iec61850.chapter11.l02.title: Purpose of SCL in IEC 61850 Engineering
iec61850.chapter11.l02.p01: SCL reduces repeated manual entry by describing a shared engineering model. A system configurator can combine device capabilities, allocate communication and resolve relationships, then return relevant configurations to device tools.
iec61850.chapter11.l02.p02: This benefit depends on ownership and revision discipline. Uncontrolled imports can replace a newer configuration with an old capability description or lose unsupported extensions. Every exchange must state who owns the system model and which tool is authoritative for device application settings.
iec61850.chapter11.l02.wf03: Compare returned files with the approved baseline
iec61850.chapter11.l02.example: When 33-F01 adds a new GOOSE signal, update the system configuration and all affected consumers together. Do not treat a locally edited CID as the new station master by default.
iec61850.chapter11.l02.check: Document which information survives each tool round trip and verify that unsupported elements are not silently discarded.
iec61850.chapter11.l03.title: SCL XML Structure
iec61850.chapter11.l03.p01: XML represents information through nested elements, attributes and references. In SCL, the root namespace and version information identify the language context, while named types and instances connect the model's structure.
iec61850.chapter11.l03.p02: Well-formed XML requires valid nesting and quoting; schema validity adds rules about allowed elements and values. Semantic validity goes further by checking that references resolve and that the engineered meaning is consistent. These are three different validation stages.
iec61850.chapter11.l03.wf01: Parse the XML without external entity expansion
iec61850.chapter11.l03.wf02: Validate against the selected IEC schema
iec61850.chapter11.l03.wf03: Resolve type, device and communication references
iec61850.chapter11.l03.example: An LN instance can name lnType="XCBR_Type" while no matching LNodeType exists. The file may be well formed but cannot provide a complete type definition for that instance.
iec61850.chapter11.l03.check: Do not claim full schema validation from a generic XML parser; record the schema edition and validation tool used.
iec61850.chapter11.l04.title: IEC 61850-6 Overview
iec61850.chapter11.l04.p01: IEC 61850-6 defines the engineering configuration language and exchange framework. Its edition and amendments matter because supported elements, file roles and engineering features evolve over time.
iec61850.chapter11.l04.p02: The project must agree compatible editions across system and IED tools. Automatically upgrading a file's version text does not convert unsupported content correctly. Vendor extensions may be useful, but their meaning and portability require documented support.
iec61850.chapter11.l04.wf03: Test representative exchanges before configuring every bay
iec61850.chapter11.l04.example: The station integrator exchanges one representative feeder configuration with each vendor tool. Any lost report, GOOSE binding or application reference is resolved before copying the pattern to remaining feeders.
iec61850.chapter11.l04.check: Use the applicable schema and device capability documentation; never infer compatibility from an .scd filename alone.
iec61850.chapter11.l05.title: ICD File — IED Capability Description
iec61850.chapter11.l05.p01: An ICD file describes an IED's capabilities for engineering use. It can include the available information model and supported communication services, providing a starting point for system integration.
iec61850.chapter11.l05.p02: An ICD is not necessarily the final instantiated station configuration. Optional functions, application selection and firmware can affect the exported model. Collect the file that matches the intended hardware, firmware and configured functional scope rather than reusing a generic library file without verification.
iec61850.chapter11.l05.wf02: Export or obtain its supported capability description
iec61850.chapter11.l05.wf03: Compare required functions and service limits with the project schedule
iec61850.chapter11.l05.example: For 33-F01, confirm the required measurement and control objects exist in the selected ICD before assigning gateway tags or GOOSE DataSet members.
iec61850.chapter11.l05.check: Archive provenance, firmware and export date with the ICD; similar product names can expose different capabilities.
iec61850.chapter11.l06.title: CID File — Configured IED Description
iec61850.chapter11.l06.p01: A CID file describes a configured IED in its engineering context. It is commonly used to transfer the relevant finalized IEC 61850 configuration to a device or its engineering tool where that workflow is supported.
iec61850.chapter11.l06.p02: A CID should not be mistaken for the complete station configuration or all proprietary protection settings. Actual download packaging and accepted file types are vendor-dependent. Check that the deployed device and the approved SCD remain consistent after the tool applies its own validation.
iec61850.chapter11.l06.wf01: Generate the device configuration from the approved system revision
iec61850.chapter11.l06.wf02: Validate it in the IED tool
iec61850.chapter11.l06.wf03: Download through the supported procedure and verify the live model
iec61850.chapter11.l06.example: After configuring 33-F01 reports and GOOSE, compare live stream identity and DataSet membership with the exported CID and station SCD.
iec61850.chapter11.l06.check: Retain the full vendor project when required; a CID alone may not restore protection settings, logic or hardware allocation.
iec61850.chapter11.l07.title: SCD File — Substation Configuration Description
iec61850.chapter11.l07.p01: An SCD file describes the configured substation system and relationships among participating IEDs. It coordinates models, communication parameters and engineered exchanges across the station.
iec61850.chapter11.l07.p02: The SCD is a controlled system artifact. It does not automatically replace switch configuration files, protection studies or vendor application projects. Changes to a publisher or address allocation may affect several devices, so revision review must consider all consumers.
iec61850.chapter11.l07.wf01: Establish the SCD baseline and owner
iec61850.chapter11.l07.wf03: Validate dependencies and distribute affected device configurations
iec61850.chapter11.l07.example: Adding a new trip member to 33-F01 requires checking every subscriber, not only exporting another file for the publisher. Gateway mappings may also depend on the changed model.
iec61850.chapter11.l07.check: Preserve an as-built SCD that matches tested device configurations rather than only the original design-stage file.
iec61850.chapter11.l08.title: IID File — Instantiated IED Description
iec61850.chapter11.l08.p01: An IID file supports exchange of an instantiated IED description in the system engineering process. It can convey changes associated with a particular device instance back into the coordinated system model.
iec61850.chapter11.l08.p02: This role helps iterative engineering, but tool support and merge behavior must be checked. Importing an IID should not silently overwrite unrelated station settings. Treat the exchange as a reviewed change with identifiable source and target revisions.
iec61850.chapter11.l08.wf01: Export the changed IED instance using the supported workflow
iec61850.chapter11.l08.wf03: Merge into the system configuration and revalidate dependent exchanges
iec61850.chapter11.l08.example: If 33-F01's application gains another available logical node, the integrator evaluates its IID update before assigning new DataSets or subscriber references.
iec61850.chapter11.l08.check: Confirm the tool preserves previously engineered addressing and bindings; file acceptance does not prove a correct merge.
iec61850.chapter11.l09.title: SSD File — System Specification Description
iec61850.chapter11.l09.p01: An SSD file expresses system specification information, including substation structure and intended functions as supported by the engineering process. It helps establish what the system should do before all concrete device instances are assigned.
iec61850.chapter11.l09.p02: Specification and implementation are different stages. A logical function in the specification must eventually be allocated to supported IED capabilities and connected to physical equipment. The SSD does not prove that those devices have been configured or commissioned.
iec61850.chapter11.l09.wf01: Define voltage levels, bays and functional requirements
iec61850.chapter11.l09.wf02: Review the specification against the single-line diagram
iec61850.chapter11.l09.example: The 132/33/11 kV project specifies line, transformer and feeder functions before assigning particular relay variants. The final SCD records the chosen instantiated solution.
iec61850.chapter11.l09.check: Maintain traceability from specification requirements to implemented functions and acceptance tests, not just file-to-file conversion history.
iec61850.chapter11.l10.title: SCL File Types Comparison
iec61850.chapter11.l10.p01: SCL file extensions indicate engineering roles, not arbitrary interchangeable formats. ICD describes capabilities, IID an instantiated device exchange, CID a configured device, SCD the configured system and SSD the system specification.
iec61850.chapter11.l10.p02: Renaming an extension does not create the missing content or validate the new role. Tools may accept subsets or proprietary packages, so confirm the documented workflow. The project should identify authoritative files and avoid distributing several conflicting versions as equally current.
iec61850.chapter11.l10.wf01: Match each engineering deliverable to its role
iec61850.chapter11.l10.wf03: Verify content and revision before exchange
iec61850.chapter11.l10.example: The integrator uses an ICD to begin 33-F01 integration, an approved SCD to coordinate the station, and the supported device output for deployment. Those artifacts are retained for different purposes.
iec61850.chapter11.l10.check: Never replace the station master with a single-device export merely because both files contain an SCL root element.
iec61850.chapter11.l11.title: Header and Substation Sections
iec61850.chapter11.l11.p01: The Header section carries identification and revision information relevant to engineering control. The Substation section describes the electrical structure and associations between primary equipment and logical functions where represented.
iec61850.chapter11.l11.p02: Equipment names and connectivity should align with approved drawings. A syntactically valid bay name that refers to the wrong feeder can create dangerous operational confusion. Revision metadata must also reflect controlled changes rather than remaining at an uninformative default forever.
iec61850.chapter11.l11.wf01: Compare substation, voltage-level and bay names with drawings
iec61850.chapter11.l11.wf03: Update revision history through the agreed process
iec61850.chapter11.l11.example: 33-F01 belongs to the 33 kV voltage level, while 11-F01 belongs to the 11 kV system supplied through the defined 33/11 kV transformer in the practical project.
iec61850.chapter11.l11.check: Do not connect 11 kV feeders directly to a 33 kV bus in the specification merely to simplify the drawing.
iec61850.chapter11.l12.title: IED and AccessPoint Sections
iec61850.chapter11.l12.p01: The IED element identifies a device instance; AccessPoint describes an access arrangement through which relevant services are exposed. Within server content, logical devices contain logical nodes linked to type definitions.
iec61850.chapter11.l12.p02: Names, logical-device instances and optional explicit naming features influence the exposed references. Do not universally assume every domain name is a simple concatenation without checking the actual configuration. Multiple access points may have distinct roles or supported services.
iec61850.chapter11.l12.wf01: Locate the intended IED and AccessPoint
iec61850.chapter11.l12.wf02: Trace Server, LDevice and LN instances
iec61850.chapter11.l12.wf03: Compare the resulting references with the online model
iec61850.chapter11.l12.example: The tutorial assumes IED_33_F01 and LDevice inst LD0 expose IED_33_F01LD0. This convention is stated explicitly and must be verified before importing real gateway tags.
iec61850.chapter11.l12.check: Check access-point references in Communication as well as the IED model; a correct device name with the wrong access point still fails integration.
iec61850.chapter11.l13.title: Communication Section
iec61850.chapter11.l13.p01: The Communication section describes network associations and addressing for connected access points and supported communication services. GSE and SMV entries associate Ethernet parameters with particular logical-device control blocks.
iec61850.chapter11.l13.p02: A network address is only useful if its IED, access point, logical device and control-block references resolve. Numeric representation also matters: tools may display decimal VLAN values while SCL uses the specified hexadecimal representation for an address parameter.
iec61850.chapter11.l13.wf01: Resolve each ConnectedAP to an IED/AccessPoint
iec61850.chapter11.l13.wf02: Validate IP and service address allocations
iec61850.chapter11.l13.wf03: Compare the exported values with live traffic
iec61850.chapter11.l13.example: The illustrative gcbTrip stream uses VLAN decimal 200, represented as 0C8 in its SCL VLAN-ID field. Its APPID 1001 is explicitly hexadecimal in the address example.
iec61850.chapter11.l13.check: Check the station allocation register for duplicates and verify that switch VLAN configuration uses the intended numeric value.
iec61850.chapter11.l14.title: DataTypeTemplates Section
iec61850.chapter11.l14.p01: DataTypeTemplates defines reusable logical-node, data-object, data-attribute and enumeration types. Instances refer to these definitions rather than repeating every structural detail in the device tree.
iec61850.chapter11.l14.p02: Type references must resolve consistently. A correctly named data object with the wrong common data class or attribute type can break client decoding or subscriber mapping. Vendor namespaces and extensions require explicit handling instead of silently substituting a familiar standard type.
iec61850.chapter11.l14.wf03: Verify functional constraints and enumeration meanings against the intended model
iec61850.chapter11.l14.example: For an illustrative XCBR1.Pos, the position object's type must support the expected double-point semantics and relevant attributes. A generic Boolean substitute would lose intermediate and bad-state information.
iec61850.chapter11.l14.check: Validate structure and meaning together; identical object names do not guarantee identical supported attributes or control behavior.
iec61850.chapter11.l15.title: DataSet and ReportControl Elements
iec61850.chapter11.l15.p01: DataSet elements list selected functional-constrained data in a defined order. ReportControl binds a report configuration to its DataSet and specifies supported triggers, optional fields and timing parameters.
iec61850.chapter11.l15.p02: An FCDA element can identify an object-level selection when the attribute name is omitted appropriately; its name alone does not mean every entry is a scalar attribute. Fragment examples need the surrounding LN0, data model and type definitions before they can form a deployable file.
iec61850.chapter11.l15.wf02: Check ReportControl datSet and configuration revision
iec61850.chapter11.l15.wf03: Verify trigger behavior and actual client decoding
iec61850.chapter11.l15.example: The example dsStatus selects XCBR1.Pos at ST and binds a buffered report. The client checks returned structure and inclusion rather than assuming separate stVal, q and t scalar entries.
iec61850.chapter11.l15.check: Use vendor-supported reporting limits and reserve instances deliberately; arbitrary XML does not create unsupported server resources.
iec61850.chapter11.l16.title: GSEControl and SampledValueControl
iec61850.chapter11.l16.p01: GSEControl and SampledValueControl describe different communication services. GOOSE publishes application state with retransmission; SV publishes a measurement sample stream according to its selected profile.
iec61850.chapter11.l16.p02: Both require appropriate DataSets, communication entries and compatible consumers, but their rates, payload interpretation and supervision differ. Do not copy a GOOSE block and merely rename it to configure Sampled Values. Profile-specific SV fields require exact device support.
iec61850.chapter11.l16.wf01: Identify the service and publisher control block
iec61850.chapter11.l16.wf02: Resolve its DataSet and Communication entry
iec61850.chapter11.l16.wf03: Validate receiver compatibility and deployed stream fields
iec61850.chapter11.l16.example: 33-F01 gcbTrip is a GOOSE application stream, while MU_132_L01 publishes an SV measurement stream. Their identifiers and network allocations are managed separately.
iec61850.chapter11.l16.check: Check sample profile and channel mapping for SV; check ordered state data and application binding for GOOSE.
iec61850.chapter11.l17.title: ExtRef and GOOSE Subscription Engineering
iec61850.chapter11.l17.p01: ExtRef elements express dependencies on external data sources. In GOOSE engineering they identify the source information needed by a receiving logical function, with additional control-block context where supported and required by the edition.
iec61850.chapter11.l17.p02: A resolved external reference does not necessarily complete the proprietary internal logic binding. Tools may require an explicit association to an internal signal name. Verify that the received member reaches the correct function and that quality and communication supervision are handled.
iec61850.chapter11.l17.wf01: Resolve source IED, LD, LN and attribute
iec61850.chapter11.l17.wf03: Confirm the internal receiving signal changes during an isolated functional test
iec61850.chapter11.l17.example: The subscriber consumes the approved 33-F01 trip member. Its import report, online subscription diagnostic and application input are all compared with the system signal matrix.
iec61850.chapter11.l17.check: After a publisher rename or member-order change, revalidate every dependent ExtRef and application binding.
iec61850.chapter11.l18.title: SCL Import and Export Workflow
iec61850.chapter11.l18.p01: Reliable SCL exchange is a controlled round trip between system and device tools. Begin from known source revisions, import only supported content, review differences and export a traceable result.
iec61850.chapter11.l18.p02: Tool warnings can reveal dropped elements, unsupported editions or unresolved references. Ignoring them may produce files that look plausible but no longer represent the approved system. Keep a reversible baseline and compare meaningful model changes instead of relying only on file size.
iec61850.chapter11.l18.wf03: Export, compare and functionally verify the affected services
iec61850.chapter11.l18.example: After a 33-F01 update, compare DataSets, reports, GOOSE identities and subscriber references before distributing the new SCD-derived configurations.
iec61850.chapter11.l18.check: Do not merge concurrent station edits by replacing whole files blindly; resolve ownership and dependencies before accepting either revision.
iec61850.chapter11.l19.title: Practical Multi-Vendor SCD Engineering
iec61850.chapter11.l19.p01: Multi-vendor SCD engineering integrates supported device models into one coherent station configuration. The integrator coordinates names, addresses, reports and inter-IED exchanges while vendors retain responsibility for their device-specific application settings.
iec61850.chapter11.l19.p02: A pilot integration exposes edition differences, naming conventions and import limitations before repetition across many bays. Use representative devices and actual firmware, and retain an interoperability matrix covering both positive functions and failure behavior.
iec61850.chapter11.l19.wf02: Integrate one representative bay from each vendor
iec61850.chapter11.l19.wf03: Resolve exchanges and repeat joint acceptance tests
iec61850.chapter11.l19.example: The 33 kV pilot includes a protection publisher, another vendor's subscriber and a gateway MMS client. Every signal has a source reference, destination binding, expected type and test case.
iec61850.chapter11.l19.check: Conformance certificates support capability review but do not replace testing the delivered combination of tools, settings and applications.
iec61850.chapter11.l20.title: SCL Validation and Troubleshooting
iec61850.chapter11.l20.p01: SCL troubleshooting should distinguish malformed XML, schema violations, unresolved references, unsupported capabilities and inconsistent application meaning. Each class requires different evidence and a different correction.
iec61850.chapter11.l20.p02: Validate from the smallest failing relationship outward. A report referencing a nonexistent DataSet should be repaired before investigating the gateway network. A schema-valid GOOSE subscription that never changes internal logic requires checking binding and live stream identity.
iec61850.chapter11.l20.wf02: Resolve the referenced element and its dependencies
iec61850.chapter11.l20.wf03: Revalidate the file and repeat the affected runtime test
iec61850.chapter11.l20.example: If 33-F01's gcbTrip points to an obsolete DataSet name, correct the coordinated system revision and regenerate the endpoint configurations. Do not patch only the displayed name in the receiver.
iec61850.chapter11.l20.check: Archive the final validation report, exported files and device evidence so future engineers can reproduce the tested configuration.
iec61850.chapter12.l01.title: Introduction to IED Engineering
iec61850.chapter12.l01.p01: IED engineering translates protection, control and communication requirements into a verified device configuration. It includes hardware allocation, application settings, information models and integration with the station system.
iec61850.chapter12.l01.p02: A relay that communicates successfully can still have incorrect protection settings or physical I/O mapping. Treat each domain as a controlled configuration with linked tests. The device's hardware, firmware and licensed functions determine what can actually be implemented.
iec61850.chapter12.l01.wf01: Review the protection and control requirements
iec61850.chapter12.l01.wf03: Configure, test and archive the integrated result
iec61850.chapter12.l01.example: 33-F01 requires feeder protection, breaker feedback, approved control and station reporting. These functions are allocated before network addresses or DataSets are finalized.
iec61850.chapter12.l01.check: Keep the protection settings file, vendor application project and IEC 61850 export together; none alone necessarily restores the complete IED.
iec61850.chapter12.l02.title: Protection IED Hardware Architecture
iec61850.chapter12.l02.p01: A protection IED typically combines measurement inputs, processing, binary I/O, communication interfaces, auxiliary supply and a local operator interface. The exact module arrangement and isolation ratings are product-specific.
iec61850.chapter12.l02.p02: Hardware allocation affects software engineering. An optional Ethernet module or binary output card cannot be assumed present from the product family name. Check terminal schedules and module identification before assigning a signal to a nonexistent channel.
iec61850.chapter12.l02.wf03: Verify physical interfaces during inspection and testing
iec61850.chapter12.l02.example: For 33-F01, the approved output assigned to the trip circuit is identified by its actual terminal and contact duty. The IEC 61850 trip indication is linked to that function but is not the physical contact itself.
iec61850.chapter12.l02.check: Confirm auxiliary power and contact ratings from the installed variant, not a generic catalogue photograph.
iec61850.chapter12.l03.title: IED Configuration Software Overview
iec61850.chapter12.l03.p01: Vendor engineering software configures supported protection settings, logic, hardware and communication. Tool versions, device connectivity packages and firmware compatibility influence what can be opened, edited and downloaded.
iec61850.chapter12.l03.p02: Use documented procedures without assuming common menu names across vendors. Opening an old project in a newer tool can trigger conversion, so preserve the original and review the conversion report. A tool-generated configuration still requires functional validation.
iec61850.chapter12.l03.wf01: Install the approved tool/device package combination
iec61850.chapter12.l03.example: The 33-F01 configuration is edited using the package validated for its firmware. The engineer records the tool version with the final backup to support future maintenance.
iec61850.chapter12.l03.check: Do not overwrite the only working project during an automatic conversion; retain a recoverable baseline and compare changed settings.
iec61850.chapter12.l04.title: IED Network Parameter Configuration
iec61850.chapter12.l04.p01: Network configuration establishes device identity and reachability. Address, mask, gateway, interface role and redundancy mode must align with the station plan and supported hardware.
iec61850.chapter12.l04.p02: Two Ethernet ports do not necessarily mean PRP support; they may be switched, redundant, independent or dedicated to different services. Configuration must follow the device manual. Duplicate IP addresses can produce intermittent connections that look like random protocol faults.
iec61850.chapter12.l04.wf01: Assign a unique address and interface role
iec61850.chapter12.l04.wf03: Test the intended client path and inspect address conflicts
iec61850.chapter12.l04.example: 33-F01 uses 192.168.100.31/24 in the illustrative station plan. Its protection GOOSE VLAN allocation is recorded separately because conventional GOOSE does not depend on that IP address.
iec61850.chapter12.l04.check: Confirm the active physical port and mode after download; a correct setting on an unused interface will not restore communication.
iec61850.chapter12.l05.title: Logical Device and Logical Node Configuration
iec61850.chapter12.l05.p01: Logical devices group application information, and logical nodes represent standardized functional concepts. The exposed model depends on configured functions, supported templates and vendor naming conventions.
iec61850.chapter12.l05.p02: Engineering must connect the model to real equipment. A logical node named XCBR1 may represent a specific breaker only within the device's defined application. Renaming nodes without coordinating consumers can invalidate reports, controls and subscriptions.
iec61850.chapter12.l05.wf02: Associate each logical node with equipment/function
iec61850.chapter12.l05.wf03: Verify the online references against the approved signal list
iec61850.chapter12.l05.example: The tutorial maps 33-F01 breaker feedback to IED_33_F01LD0/XCBR1.Pos. Actual prefixes, instances and logical-device naming must be read from the delivered configuration.
iec61850.chapter12.l05.check: Do not create unsupported logical nodes merely to make a generic training reference appear in a vendor tool.
iec61850.chapter12.l06.title: DataSet Configuration
iec61850.chapter12.l06.p01: DataSet engineering selects information for reports or multicast services. Member order, functional constraint and structure must match the intended consumer and fit the device's documented limits.
iec61850.chapter12.l06.p02: Group data by service purpose and update behavior. A protection GOOSE DataSet and an operator measurement report have different timing and semantic requirements. Oversized DataSets can waste bandwidth and complicate decoding without improving visibility.
iec61850.chapter12.l06.wf01: Build the point list for one service
iec61850.chapter12.l06.wf02: Select supported members in a controlled order
iec61850.chapter12.l06.wf03: Verify types, capacity and consumer interpretation
iec61850.chapter12.l06.example: 33-F01 uses a status-oriented DataSet for breaker and protection indications and a separate measurement acquisition arrangement. The exact grouping is chosen from the project's update and retention requirements.
iec61850.chapter12.l06.check: After any membership change, coordinate revisions and repeat client/subscriber tests; do not update the publisher alone.
iec61850.chapter12.l07.title: Report Control Block Configuration
iec61850.chapter12.l07.p01: RCB configuration determines how selected data reaches an MMS reporting client. Relevant settings include buffered behavior, DataSet association, triggers, optional fields and timing, subject to the IED's supported implementation.
iec61850.chapter12.l07.p02: Allocate report instances to clients deliberately. Ownership conflicts or an enabled block can prevent reconfiguration. Buffered reports have finite storage and require client recovery logic; enabling a BRCB does not guarantee unlimited historical coverage.
iec61850.chapter12.l07.wf03: Test event, GI, integrity and reconnection behavior
iec61850.chapter12.l07.example: Gateway A receives 33-F01 status through its allocated buffered report. Gateway B uses a documented independent resource or supported redundancy arrangement rather than repeatedly taking Gateway A's block.
iec61850.chapter12.l07.check: Record retention assumptions and overflow handling in the acceptance plan, including how the HMI indicates a possible event gap.
iec61850.chapter12.l08.title: GOOSE Publisher Configuration
iec61850.chapter12.l08.p01: GOOSE publisher engineering binds an application DataSet to a control block and network allocation. The published values must correspond to actual application signals, including the defined operating and test modes.
iec61850.chapter12.l08.p02: Correct APPID and MAC settings cannot compensate for a DataSet member bound to the wrong internal protection result. Validate the source condition first, then verify the transmitted payload and counters. Export the final publisher description for all consumers.
iec61850.chapter12.l08.wf01: Map the internal source signal to the exposed model
iec61850.chapter12.l08.wf03: Inject the source and compare the live stream
iec61850.chapter12.l08.example: 33-F01 publishes the approved trip member through gcbTrip using APPID 0x1001 and VLAN 200 in the illustrative exercise. Both the source Boolean and quality handling are verified.
iec61850.chapter12.l08.check: Distinguish a protection start indication from an operate/trip indication; publishing the wrong stage changes scheme behavior.
iec61850.chapter12.l09.title: GOOSE Subscriber Configuration
iec61850.chapter12.l09.p01: Subscriber engineering links an external GOOSE member to an internal application input. It requires agreement on stream identity, configuration revision, member order and data type, followed by a documented vendor-specific binding.
iec61850.chapter12.l09.p02: The subscriber must supervise stream freshness and handle invalid quality according to the protection or control design. A communication diagnostic showing received frames is only one stage; the internal signal and resulting application behavior must also be observed.
iec61850.chapter12.l09.wf02: Resolve external references and bind inputs
iec61850.chapter12.l09.wf03: Test valid, missing and mismatched streams
iec61850.chapter12.l09.example: The receiving controller maps 33-F01's trip member into a designated isolated test input. A separate diagnostic supervises the stream so a communication failure is not silently interpreted as a valid false value.
iec61850.chapter12.l09.check: Retest the internal binding after every import or firmware change that modifies the receiving application.
iec61850.chapter12.l10.title: Time Synchronization Configuration
iec61850.chapter12.l10.p01: IED time configuration selects a supported source and defines how the device reports synchronization health. SNTP, PTP and other timing interfaces have different accuracy and network requirements.
iec61850.chapter12.l10.p02: Match the required time performance to the application. SOE timestamping and multi-source sampled-value alignment may need different designs. A displayed correct wall clock does not prove acceptable offset, holdover or timestamp quality.
iec61850.chapter12.l10.wf01: Select the approved timing method and source
iec61850.chapter12.l10.wf02: Configure supported profile/domain or server parameters
iec61850.chapter12.l10.wf03: Verify offset, quality and failure behavior
iec61850.chapter12.l10.example: 33-F01 uses the project's approved station time source for events. A merging unit requiring precise sample alignment uses its compatible PTP profile rather than assuming the feeder's SNTP settings are sufficient.
iec61850.chapter12.l10.check: Check source time and quality after restart and reference loss; do not assess timing only from the HMI's local clock display.
iec61850.chapter12.l11.title: Binary Input and Output Mapping
iec61850.chapter12.l11.p01: Binary-input mapping translates terminal states into application signals; binary-output mapping links logic to physical contacts. Debounce, inversion, contact type and supervision affect the resulting behavior.
iec61850.chapter12.l11.p02: The signal schedule must distinguish electrical contact state from process meaning. A normally closed alarm contact can require inversion, while breaker position commonly combines two auxiliary contacts to detect intermediate or inconsistent states. Do not force every status into one Boolean.
iec61850.chapter12.l11.wf03: Test every state through the model and output indication
iec61850.chapter12.l11.example: 33-F01's 52a and 52b inputs produce XCBR1.Pos through the approved double-point logic. Test open, closed and abnormal combinations before accepting the HMI display.
iec61850.chapter12.l11.check: Use isolated approved test interfaces; a laptop network connection is not a substitute for correctly rated binary-input test equipment.
iec61850.chapter12.l12.title: Analog Measurement Mapping
iec61850.chapter12.l12.p01: Analog measurement mapping connects physical or sampled inputs to engineering quantities and published objects. Ratios, nominal ratings, units, phase sequence and sign conventions determine whether the values have operational meaning.
iec61850.chapter12.l12.p02: Scaling can occur in the IED and again in the gateway. Applying a CT ratio twice can produce a plausible but grossly wrong display. Document where primary conversion occurs and verify multiple test points rather than a single nominal reading.
iec61850.chapter12.l12.wf03: Compare injected values, IED display and SCADA presentation
iec61850.chapter12.l12.example: For 33-F01, inject known phase currents and check the corresponding MMXU1 quantities. The gateway displays primary amperes only after confirming whether the IED already supplies primary values.
iec61850.chapter12.l12.check: Include zero, representative load and a higher test value, plus phase-angle or direction checks where relevant.
iec61850.chapter12.l13.title: Protection Trip Signal Mapping
iec61850.chapter12.l13.p01: Protection trip mapping links the intended operate condition to trip conditioning, physical outputs and communication indications. Start, operate, general trip and breaker-open feedback represent different stages and must not be conflated.
iec61850.chapter12.l13.p02: Review the protection logic and cause-and-effect matrix before assigning an IEC 61850 point. Some functions combine phases or protection elements, while others expose individual indications. Exact available objects and internal signal names are device-specific.
iec61850.chapter12.l13.wf02: Trace physical output and network indications
iec61850.chapter12.l13.wf03: Inject the protection condition and verify every intended destination
iec61850.chapter12.l13.example: An illustrative chain is PTOC operate to PTRC trip conditioning to the assigned breaker output. XCBR1.Pos then reports actual breaker feedback, which may remain closed if the mechanism fails.
iec61850.chapter12.l13.check: Test unwanted destinations remain inactive; correct operation of one contact does not prove the mapping has no unintended parallel output.
iec61850.chapter12.l14.title: Control and Interlocking Configuration
iec61850.chapter12.l14.p01: Control engineering combines command authority, the object's control model, permissives, interlocks and physical output logic. The operator request and protection trip path may have different conditions and priorities.
iec61850.chapter12.l14.p02: Configure the approved switching philosophy rather than a generic set of interlocks. Missing or invalid remote inputs require an explicit response. The operator should receive a meaningful rejection or failure indication without losing independent protection capability.
iec61850.chapter12.l14.wf03: Test allowed, rejected, local-mode and timeout cases
iec61850.chapter12.l14.example: 33-F01 remote closing uses the supported CSWI control object and independently verifies breaker position. A stale remote earth-switch indication is handled according to the approved fail-safe policy.
iec61850.chapter12.l14.check: Do not use a maintenance override as the normal solution to a rejected close; identify and resolve the failed condition.
iec61850.chapter12.l15.title: ICD/CID/SCD Import and Export
iec61850.chapter12.l15.p01: ICD, IID, SCD and CID exchanges serve different stages of IED integration. The chosen workflow must preserve both standardized communication information and the vendor application's supported bindings.
iec61850.chapter12.l15.p02: File imports can alter names, control blocks or model options. Review diagnostic messages and compare the result with the system baseline before download. Keep the complete vendor project because SCL may not contain every protection or hardware setting.
iec61850.chapter12.l15.wf02: Import the approved exchange file and resolve diagnostics
iec61850.chapter12.l15.wf03: Export the resulting configuration and compare live behavior
iec61850.chapter12.l15.example: After importing the station SCD for 33-F01, verify its reports, GOOSE subscriptions and time/network parameters in the deployed device. Do not rely solely on the tool's import-success dialog.
iec61850.chapter12.l15.check: Record the exact station and device revisions used for testing so another engineer can reproduce the result.
iec61850.chapter12.l16.title: Multi-Vendor IED Integration
iec61850.chapter12.l16.p01: Multi-vendor IED integration requires semantic agreement as well as transport compatibility. Device editions, optional attributes, control models, reporting limits and engineering-tool behavior can differ.
iec61850.chapter12.l16.p02: A representative pilot test should expose those differences before mass configuration. Use actual firmware and capability documents and avoid inventing a common proprietary workflow. Normalize engineering documentation while preserving the exact source references used by each device.
iec61850.chapter12.l16.wf01: Collect supported models and service limits
iec61850.chapter12.l16.wf03: Test one complete inter-vendor function before repeating it
iec61850.chapter12.l16.example: One vendor's 33-F01 publisher sends a trip indication to another vendor's controller. The test verifies member type, quality, timeout and internal logic binding, not just multicast delivery.
iec61850.chapter12.l16.check: Treat any workaround as a documented design decision with repeatable tests; do not hide type conversion inside an unexplained gateway expression.
iec61850.chapter12.l17.title: SCADA Client Integration
iec61850.chapter12.l17.p01: SCADA client integration connects the IED's supported model to the station point database. Required work includes association settings, reference mapping, report allocation, quality handling, timestamps and control authorization.
iec61850.chapter12.l17.p02: Commission the points from a known physical or simulated stimulus. A green communication icon does not prove correct units, double-point states or event ordering. Test the client's behavior when the IED is unavailable or returns invalid data.
iec61850.chapter12.l17.wf03: Perform point-by-point value, quality, time and control tests
