iec61850.chapter16.l09.wf02: Map supported permissive indications and their inputs
iec61850.chapter16.l09.wf03: Test allowed and blocked states with diagnostics
iec61850.chapter16.l09.example: The example controller combines verified earth-switch and disconnector conditions with local authority before allowing the selected close action. The full condition set is project-specific.
iec61850.chapter16.l09.check: Do not assume CILO removes the need for independent mechanical or electrical interlocks required by the equipment design.
iec61850.chapter16.l10.title: Electrical and Logical Interlocking
iec61850.chapter16.l10.p01: Electrical interlocks use physical circuitry or equipment mechanisms to constrain operation; logical interlocks evaluate configured conditions in a controller or IED. A station may require both, with clearly defined responsibilities.
iec61850.chapter16.l10.p02: Their interaction must be tested. A software permissive can be true while a hardwired contact prevents coil energization, and a wiring error can undermine an assumed electrical constraint. Document the intended command path and feedback at each boundary.
iec61850.chapter16.l10.wf01: Review electrical drawings and logic together
iec61850.chapter16.l10.wf03: Test each blocking condition and the final permitted path
iec61850.chapter16.l10.example: 33-F01 close logic may require a healthy local condition while the physical circuit includes approved mechanism contacts. The tutorial shows functional stages without prescribing a universal wiring circuit.
iec61850.chapter16.l10.check: Do not defeat a physical interlock to make a software test pass; investigate the reason and follow the approved isolation procedure.
iec61850.chapter16.l11.title: Breaker Close Permissive Conditions
iec61850.chapter16.l11.p01: Close permissives prevent an operation when the required electrical, mechanical or operational conditions are not satisfied. Possible inputs include authority, earth-switch state, mechanism readiness and synchronism conditions where the scheme requires them.
iec61850.chapter16.l11.p02: The complete list comes from the approved switching philosophy. A feeder close and a bus-coupler close may have different requirements. Invalid or stale input data must have an explicit policy rather than defaulting silently to permission.
iec61850.chapter16.l11.wf02: Define each input's source and validity rule
iec61850.chapter16.l11.wf03: Test each individual block and the fully permitted case
iec61850.chapter16.l11.example: For the 33-F01 exercise, remote authority and valid approved equipment-state conditions are required. This is an illustrative subset, not a design instruction for every feeder.
iec61850.chapter16.l11.check: Show the failed permissive to the operator where supported; a generic 'command failed' message obscures the engineering cause.
iec61850.chapter16.l12.title: Breaker Trip and Open Commands
iec61850.chapter16.l12.p01: An operator open command and a protection trip can act on the same breaker through different logic paths. Their authority, permissive and priority requirements must be defined separately.
iec61850.chapter16.l12.p02: Closing interlocks should not be copied automatically into trip logic. Some operational restrictions may apply to manual commands while protection retains the required ability to clear faults. Physical trip-circuit supervision and independent feedback remain essential.
iec61850.chapter16.l12.wf01: Trace operator open and protection trip paths separately
iec61850.chapter16.l12.wf03: Test each path and its failure indications
iec61850.chapter16.l12.example: 33-F01's protection operation drives the approved trip output and reports the event. A remote open request follows the supported control model and operator authority checks.
iec61850.chapter16.l12.check: Verify the design does not let a lost HMI or stale close-permissive input disable required fault-clearing behavior.
iec61850.chapter16.l13.title: Disconnector and Earth Switch Interlocking
iec61850.chapter16.l13.p01: Disconnectors and earth switches have switching duties and interlocking requirements different from circuit breakers. Their permitted operations depend on equipment ratings, circuit conditions and the station's approved operating sequence.
iec61850.chapter16.l13.p02: Do not assume a disconnector can interrupt load or that an earth switch may close based only on one remote Boolean. Position, isolation and other required conditions must be verified through the actual scheme, including mechanical constraints where present.
iec61850.chapter16.l13.wf01: Review equipment duties and switching sequence
iec61850.chapter16.l13.wf03: Test prohibited combinations and invalid feedback in an isolated arrangement
iec61850.chapter16.l13.example: The practical project treats earth-switch information as one required input to relevant bay operations. It does not prescribe a universal live switching sequence.
iec61850.chapter16.l13.check: Use approved operating procedures and qualified personnel for site operations; the training logic does not replace equipment-specific instructions.
iec61850.chapter16.l14.title: Control Authority and Origin
iec61850.chapter16.l14.p01: Control authority identifies who may request an action, while origin information helps describe the request source and context in supported IEC 61850 control services. Authentication, application roles and origin fields are related but not interchangeable.
iec61850.chapter16.l14.p02: An origin category alone is not proof that a user is authorized. The station's access-control and operating policy must enforce permissions. Logs should retain enough context to investigate rejected, completed and uncertain commands.
iec61850.chapter16.l14.wf02: Configure supported origin and access behavior
iec61850.chapter16.l14.wf03: Test competing sources and unauthorized requests
iec61850.chapter16.l14.example: The station HMI and remote control centre have explicitly assigned authority for 33-F01. A maintenance client may browse data while being prohibited from switching.
iec61850.chapter16.l14.check: Do not trust a freely supplied origin label as the only security control; use the supported station access architecture.
iec61850.chapter16.l15.title: Command Feedback and Timeout
iec61850.chapter16.l15.p01: Command feedback includes service acceptance/rejection, additional diagnostics where supported and independent equipment position. Timeout handling determines what the client does when a definitive result is not received in the expected interval.
iec61850.chapter16.l15.p02: A timeout can mean the request failed, the response was lost or the equipment moved without timely feedback. Treat it as uncertainty until the actual state is reconciled. Repeating a command without that check can create an unintended operation.
iec61850.chapter16.l15.wf01: Set project-approved response and feedback limits
iec61850.chapter16.l15.wf03: Compare command logs with actual position before recovery
iec61850.chapter16.l15.example: 33-F01 receives a close request during an isolated test, but feedback is withheld. The HMI reports the failed/uncertain result and does not display closed merely because the request was accepted.
iec61850.chapter16.l15.check: Keep service timeout and mechanism travel/feedback timeout as separate parameters where the implementation supports them.
iec61850.chapter16.l16.title: Control Failure Handling
iec61850.chapter16.l16.p01: Control failures require a clear, non-ambiguous operator result and retained diagnostic evidence. Reasons can include authority, selection expiry, interlocking, unsupported service, output failure or missing feedback.
iec61850.chapter16.l16.p02: The response should guide investigation without bypassing constraints. A retry policy must account for the possibility that the first action already occurred. Enhanced command diagnostics can help, but physical state and application logs remain necessary.
iec61850.chapter16.l16.wf01: Capture the exact rejection or timeout
iec61850.chapter16.l16.wf03: Correct the cause and perform a new authorized test
iec61850.chapter16.l16.example: If 33-F01 rejects closing because local mode is active, the operator follows the approved authority-transfer process. The engineer does not simply disable the local check in logic.
iec61850.chapter16.l16.check: Test that a failed command cannot remain queued and execute unexpectedly when a permissive later changes.
iec61850.chapter16.l17.title: Practical Example — 33 kV Feeder Closing
iec61850.chapter16.l17.p01: The feeder-close exercise demonstrates a complete controlled transaction using an isolated breaker simulator or approved test arrangement. It verifies authority, current state, supported control model, interlocks and independent feedback.
iec61850.chapter16.l17.p02: Use the actual configured object references and timings. The exercise must include rejection and uncertainty cases so a positive result is not the only behavior taught. Record both the command-service outcome and the simulated physical position.
iec61850.chapter16.l17.wf01: Confirm the 33-F01 identity and approved permissives
iec61850.chapter16.l17.wf03: Verify position, SOE and absence of unintended outputs
iec61850.chapter16.l17.example: For an SBO-enabled CSWI1.Pos example, select then operate close while the selection is valid. XCBR1.Pos confirms the result; an expired selection or invalid permissive is rejected.
iec61850.chapter16.l17.check: This is a training sequence, not authorization for live switching; actual station operations use the approved procedure and responsible operator.
iec61850.chapter16.l18.title: Practical Example — Bus Coupler Interlocking
iec61850.chapter16.l18.p01: Bus-coupler control depends on bus topology, source conditions and the operating philosophy. Closing can parallel sources or energize a bus section, so its permissives may differ substantially from feeder switching.
iec61850.chapter16.l18.p02: Synchronism checking, dead-bus conditions and disconnector states must be included where the approved scheme requires them. A generic 'both buses healthy' condition is insufficient. Define invalid measurement and unavailable remote-state behavior explicitly.
iec61850.chapter16.l18.wf03: Test source combinations, invalid inputs and rejection diagnostics
iec61850.chapter16.l18.example: In the practical project, 33-BC01 joins bus sections 33-B1 and 33-B2 only under its approved matrix. No universal automatic paralleling rule is assumed.
iec61850.chapter16.l18.check: Do not infer safe paralleling from equal displayed voltage magnitudes alone; the required checks depend on the actual electrical system.
iec61850.chapter16.l19.title: Control FAT/SAT Testing
iec61850.chapter16.l19.p01: Control FAT verifies service sequences, authority, interlocks, outputs and feedback in a controlled setup. SAT verifies installed wiring, equipment identity and actual station interfaces under approved test boundaries.
iec61850.chapter16.l19.p02: Negative tests are as important as successful operations. Include local mode, invalid inputs, expired selection, missing feedback and communication loss at defined stages. Confirm that independent protection behavior remains consistent with the design.
iec61850.chapter16.l19.wf03: Restore modes, remove simulations and record final configuration
iec61850.chapter16.l19.example: 33-F01 testing records requested action, object reference, service result, output and position feedback. A witness verifies that no adjacent feeder output responds.
iec61850.chapter16.l19.check: Release the test boundary only after confirming normal authority, subscriptions and physical connections are restored.
iec61850.chapter16.l20.title: Breaker Control Troubleshooting
iec61850.chapter16.l20.p01: Breaker-control troubleshooting traces the request through authority, control model, selection, interlocking, output and feedback. The first failed boundary determines the next investigation step.
iec61850.chapter16.l20.p02: Distinguish a service rejection from a physical failure after acceptance. Packet evidence can show the request and response but cannot prove coil energization or mechanism movement. Use the appropriate electrical and application diagnostics under approved conditions.
iec61850.chapter16.l20.wf02: Compare client, IED and physical-feedback evidence
iec61850.chapter16.l20.wf03: Correct the cause and repeat positive and negative tests
iec61850.chapter16.l20.example: If 33-F01 accepts a close but XCBR1.Pos remains open, inspect output logic and the approved control circuit rather than changing the MMS port. If selection fails, inspect ownership, model and timeout first.
iec61850.chapter16.l20.check: Never use repeated live command attempts as a diagnostic substitute for understanding the failure.
iec61850.chapter17.l01.title: Introduction to IEC 61850 Testing
iec61850.chapter17.l01.p01: IEC 61850 testing verifies information models, communication services and the applications that use them. Device conformance testing, interoperability testing and project acceptance testing answer different questions.
iec61850.chapter17.l01.p02: IEC 61850-10 addresses conformance techniques; FAT and SAT demonstrate the delivered system against project requirements. A certificate does not prove the installed point database, wiring or protection logic is correct. Build traceability from each requirement to an observable test result.
iec61850.chapter17.l01.wf02: Define stimulus, expected result and evidence
iec61850.chapter17.l01.wf03: Record configuration versions and repeatability conditions
iec61850.chapter17.l01.example: The 33-F01 test plan includes reporting, GOOSE and control integration in addition to the relay's independent protection tests.
iec61850.chapter17.l01.check: Keep protocol compliance evidence separate from system acceptance and physical protection-performance evidence.
iec61850.chapter17.l02.title: Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT)
iec61850.chapter17.l02.p01: Factory Acceptance Testing verifies the engineered system before shipment or site installation using a controlled representative setup. It should exercise actual configurations and relevant devices, not only static screenshots or empty HMI pages.
iec61850.chapter17.l02.p02: FAT reduces site surprises by exposing model, mapping and compatibility errors early. Any simulated equipment must be identified so untested physical interfaces remain visible in the report. Negative and recovery cases should be planned alongside normal functions.
iec61850.chapter17.l02.wf03: Execute witnessed cases and record deviations for resolution
iec61850.chapter17.l02.example: 33-F01's isolated test setup feeds known states into the IED and observes gateway, HMI and subscriber behavior. A simulated breaker is explicitly labeled in the evidence.
iec61850.chapter17.l02.check: Do not claim factory simulation proves the final site wiring or mechanical breaker operation; those require the appropriate later tests.
iec61850.chapter17.l03.title: Site Acceptance Testing (SAT)
iec61850.chapter17.l03.p01: Site Acceptance Testing verifies that installation, configuration and interfaces match the accepted design. It adds real cable routes, terminal connections, network equipment, time distribution and operational boundaries.
iec61850.chapter17.l03.p02: Site changes made after FAT must be reconciled into the configuration baseline. Testing follows approved isolation and access procedures so injected signals cannot unintentionally operate live equipment. Record what was tested physically and what remained simulated.
iec61850.chapter17.l03.wf01: Verify as-built drawings and installed identities
iec61850.chapter17.l03.wf03: Execute point, communication, control and failure tests and update records
iec61850.chapter17.l03.example: At 33-F01, SAT confirms actual auxiliary contacts, trip/control interfaces, fibre ports and HMI identity. Any corrected terminal or mapping triggers the affected repeat tests.
iec61850.chapter17.l03.check: Release the bay only after simulations, temporary links and test modes are removed and independently checked.
iec61850.chapter17.l04.title: FAT vs SAT Comparison
iec61850.chapter17.l04.p01: FAT and SAT share many functional checks but differ in environment and evidence. FAT emphasizes engineered compatibility and application behavior; SAT confirms the installed system and site-specific interfaces.
iec61850.chapter17.l04.p02: Avoid repeating every factory step mechanically while missing installation risks. Use FAT results to focus SAT, but recheck functions affected by transport, installation, configuration changes or different network paths. Neither stage replaces the protection study or equipment maintenance tests.
iec61850.chapter17.l04.wf01: Map each requirement to FAT, SAT or both
iec61850.chapter17.l04.wf02: Identify assumptions that change at site
iec61850.chapter17.l04.wf03: Define mandatory repeat tests after modifications
iec61850.chapter17.l04.example: A GOOSE publisher/subscriber pair passes FAT on a test switch. SAT still verifies the installed VLAN path, fibre connection, time conditions and final application binding.
iec61850.chapter17.l04.check: Document exclusions and dependencies explicitly; 'tested at factory' is not sufficient evidence for an interface changed during installation.
iec61850.chapter17.l05.title: Engineering Document Verification
iec61850.chapter17.l05.p01: Document verification confirms that drawings, signal lists, settings, SCD files and network schedules describe the same system. Inconsistent documents can make a technically correct test verify the wrong intended function.
iec61850.chapter17.l05.p02: Check unique equipment names, voltage levels, ratios, addresses, DataSet membership and control references. Record revision numbers and resolve discrepancies before energizing or testing outputs. The as-built record must incorporate approved corrections.
iec61850.chapter17.l05.wf03: Resolve discrepancies and freeze the test baseline
iec61850.chapter17.l05.example: 33-F01 appears consistently in the SLD, terminal schedule, IED project, gateway tag list and test sheet. A copied 33-F02 address is corrected before communication tests begin.
iec61850.chapter17.l05.check: Do not use an unapproved spreadsheet as the sole authority when it conflicts with the controlled engineering drawings.
iec61850.chapter17.l06.title: IED Configuration Verification
iec61850.chapter17.l06.p01: IED configuration verification compares the deployed device with the approved settings and application project. It includes hardware, firmware, protection parameters, logic, communication and time configuration relevant to the test scope.
iec61850.chapter17.l06.p02: A file stored on the engineering laptop may differ from what is running in the relay. Use supported comparison or readback functions and record checksums where meaningful. Protect original backups and document any tool-driven conversion.
iec61850.chapter17.l06.wf01: Identify the installed IED and firmware
iec61850.chapter17.l06.wf02: Compare deployed configuration with the baseline
iec61850.chapter17.l06.wf03: Record differences and repeat affected tests after correction
iec61850.chapter17.l06.example: Before testing 33-F01 reports, verify its online DataSet and RCB configuration matches the approved export. A successful previous download is not sufficient evidence after later site edits.
iec61850.chapter17.l06.check: Do not overwrite unknown site changes blindly; establish their origin and approval before restoring a baseline.
iec61850.chapter17.l07.title: Network Communication Testing
iec61850.chapter17.l07.p01: Network communication testing verifies actual service paths, not only link lights and ping. Include VLAN membership, multicast forwarding, IP routes, transport connectivity and relevant application exchanges.
iec61850.chapter17.l07.p02: Test under representative traffic and degraded paths. Mirror-port packet loss can be a measurement artifact, so combine captures with switch and endpoint diagnostics. Acceptance limits come from the project requirements and chosen measurement method.
iec61850.chapter17.l07.wf02: Exercise MMS, GOOSE and timing paths
iec61850.chapter17.l07.wf03: Apply planned failures and record service continuity/recovery
iec61850.chapter17.l07.example: For 33-F01, confirm MMS on VLAN 100 and the assigned GOOSE stream on VLAN 200 at the subscriber port. Repeat on each required redundant path.
iec61850.chapter17.l07.check: Do not infer GOOSE or SV delivery from a successful IP ping; they require their own Layer-2 verification.
iec61850.chapter17.l08.title: MMS Read and Write Testing
iec61850.chapter17.l08.p01: MMS read tests confirm correct references, types and returned application values. Write tests should target only approved writable attributes in an isolated configuration and verify both permitted and prohibited access.
iec61850.chapter17.l08.p02: Status values are not generic writable commands. A denied write can be the expected result of access policy, ownership or current state. Record the exact service response and restore any changed test parameter to its approved value.
iec61850.chapter17.l08.wf03: Verify rejection of a prohibited operation and restore the baseline
iec61850.chapter17.l08.example: During 33-F01 FAT, read XCBR1.Pos and test a supported report parameter using the documented sequence. Breaker control uses its own control-service test, never a write to stVal.
iec61850.chapter17.l08.check: Keep a before/after record and confirm that changing a shared resource did not interrupt another client's service.
iec61850.chapter17.l09.title: DataSet and RCB Testing
iec61850.chapter17.l09.p01: DataSet/RCB tests verify ordered membership, trigger behavior, inclusion, timestamps and client allocation. Buffered reporting additionally requires controlled interruption, recovery-position handling and overflow behavior where testable.
iec61850.chapter17.l09.p02: Use distinct stimuli for data change and quality change. GI and integrity reports are current snapshots and should not be credited as historical recovery. Report receipt must be checked through the client database and event display.
iec61850.chapter17.l09.wf02: Exercise dchg, qchg, GI and integrity
iec61850.chapter17.l09.wf03: Disconnect/reconnect and assess retained events and gaps
iec61850.chapter17.l09.example: 33-F01's assigned BRCB is tested with several known transitions during an outage. The report records which entries were recovered and how any discontinuity was displayed.
iec61850.chapter17.l09.check: Do not promise unlimited replay or persistence through reboot unless supported and specifically verified for the device.
iec61850.chapter17.l10.title: GOOSE Publisher Testing
iec61850.chapter17.l10.p01: Publisher testing proves that the intended application signal appears in the correct GOOSE stream. Check identity, member order, data types, quality, counters and retransmission behavior against the approved configuration.
iec61850.chapter17.l10.p02: A packet with the right APPID may still carry the wrong application member. Inject one known source transition and compare the local model with the payload. Keep active simulation inside the approved test boundary.
iec61850.chapter17.l10.wf02: Capture the assigned stream during a transition
iec61850.chapter17.l10.wf03: Compare payload, stNum, sqNum and configuration identity
iec61850.chapter17.l10.example: 33-F01 publishes gcbTrip with APPID 0x1001. The trip member changes only for the intended test condition, and unrelated members retain their expected values.
iec61850.chapter17.l10.check: Publisher success does not prove subscriber action; record it as one stage of the complete functional test.
iec61850.chapter17.l11.title: GOOSE Subscriber Testing
iec61850.chapter17.l11.p01: Subscriber testing verifies stream acceptance, member binding, quality supervision and application response. Both correct traffic and deliberate mismatches are needed to reveal unsafe assumptions.
iec61850.chapter17.l11.p02: Test missing stream, changed configuration revision, wrong identity and invalid data through supported isolated methods. The expected output response comes from the approved scheme. Test/simulation mode behavior must be checked for each device rather than assumed universal.
iec61850.chapter17.l11.wf01: Send the approved stream and observe internal input
iec61850.chapter17.l11.wf02: Introduce one defined mismatch or loss
iec61850.chapter17.l11.wf03: Confirm diagnostics and the required application response
iec61850.chapter17.l11.example: The receiving IED accepts 33-F01's correct trip member and drives only the isolated intended output. On stream expiry it follows the documented supervision policy and raises the required indication.
iec61850.chapter17.l11.check: Verify the internal logic input, not only a receive counter or green subscription icon.
iec61850.chapter17.l12.title: Sampled Values Testing
iec61850.chapter17.l12.p01: Sampled Values tests verify measurement identity, profile, channel order, scaling, synchronization and receiver behavior. Continuous packet reception alone does not establish accurate protection quantities.
iec61850.chapter17.l12.p02: Use known injected waveforms and suitable calibrated equipment. Check phase-selective values and angle relationships, then exercise stream or timing degradation. Distinguish actual network loss from capture limitations under high-rate traffic.
iec61850.chapter17.l12.wf01: Confirm compatible profile and stream identity
iec61850.chapter17.l12.wf02: Inject each channel and compare receiver quantities
iec61850.chapter17.l12.wf03: Test invalid samples, missing stream and time degradation
iec61850.chapter17.l12.example: MU_132_L01 supplies the line IED in the isolated process-bus test. A phase-A-only stimulus must appear on the correct protection input with the expected ratio and polarity.
iec61850.chapter17.l12.check: Never create a test failure by opening an energized CT secondary; use the approved isolation and test arrangement.
iec61850.chapter17.l13.title: Time Synchronization Testing
iec61850.chapter17.l13.p01: Time testing verifies source selection, endpoint synchronization, accuracy and quality indication. The required method depends on whether the application is SOE correlation or precise sample alignment.
iec61850.chapter17.l13.p02: Measure against an appropriate reference and state uncertainty. Test reference loss, holdover and restoration, including grandmaster transitions for the selected PTP design. A clock display with many decimal places is not evidence of accuracy.
iec61850.chapter17.l13.wf03: Interrupt the reference and observe quality, alarms and recovery
iec61850.chapter17.l13.example: 33-F01 event timestamps are checked through the HMI, while MU_132_L01 timing is assessed at the measurement application boundary. The two results use their respective acceptance limits.
iec61850.chapter17.l13.check: Retain measurement conditions and equipment calibration information with the report so another engineer can interpret the claimed performance.
iec61850.chapter17.l14.title: SCADA/HMI Signal Testing
iec61850.chapter17.l14.p01: SCADA point testing confirms that a known source stimulus reaches the correct operator tag with correct value, state, unit, quality and time. It should include every required abnormal state as well as normal indication.
iec61850.chapter17.l14.p02: Template-based databases can contain duplicated sources or incorrect scaling. Test each physical identity, not merely one representative graphic. For remote points, extend the test through the gateway protocol conversion to the control-centre display.
iec61850.chapter17.l14.wf02: Compare IED, driver, database and HMI
iec61850.chapter17.l14.wf03: Verify invalid quality, stale state and source timestamp handling
iec61850.chapter17.l14.example: 33-F01 open, closed, intermediate and bad-state indications are checked separately. Current is tested at multiple values to expose gain or offset errors.
iec61850.chapter17.l14.check: Record both source and destination observations; an HMI screenshot without a known stimulus cannot prove mapping correctness.
iec61850.chapter17.l15.title: Breaker Control and Interlocking Testing
iec61850.chapter17.l15.p01: Control testing verifies authorized requests, the supported control model, interlocks, physical output and independent feedback. It must also demonstrate that prohibited operations remain blocked.
iec61850.chapter17.l15.p02: Use an isolated breaker simulator or approved site test boundary. Include local mode, invalid permissives, selection expiry and missing feedback. Protection trip behavior is assessed separately according to the scheme, avoiding accidental application of close interlocks to trip logic.
iec61850.chapter17.l15.wf02: Execute permitted and rejected command cases
iec61850.chapter17.l15.wf03: Verify output, feedback, diagnostics and final restoration
iec61850.chapter17.l15.example: For 33-F01, the witness observes the selected control object and intended output while an adjacent feeder remains unchanged. A timeout produces uncertainty handling rather than an automatic retry.
iec61850.chapter17.l15.check: Remove test injections and verify normal authority and feedback before returning the bay to service.
iec61850.chapter17.l16.title: Alarm and SOE Testing
iec61850.chapter17.l16.p01: Alarm and SOE tests verify condition priority, source time, acknowledgment, return-to-normal and retention. They also check that repeated transport messages do not create false repeated physical events.
iec61850.chapter17.l16.p02: Test event bursts and buffered recovery, not only isolated slow transitions. Clock uncertainty and communication gaps must remain visible. Acknowledging an alarm should not clear its active condition or erase the event evidence.
iec61850.chapter17.l16.wf02: Verify event identity/time and alarm lifecycle
iec61850.chapter17.l16.wf03: Repeat during communication loss and recovery
iec61850.chapter17.l16.example: 33-F01 protection operation, breaker-open feedback and communication loss appear as distinct records. Reconnection preserves recovered source timestamps and identifies unrecoverable gaps according to the design.
iec61850.chapter17.l16.check: Check sorting and export behavior when events share timestamps or have degraded time quality; do not imply an unjustified causal order.
iec61850.chapter17.l17.title: Network Redundancy Testing
iec61850.chapter17.l17.p01: Redundancy testing verifies service continuity for the explicitly defined failure set. PRP, HSR, RSTP and server redundancy have different mechanisms and acceptance expectations.
iec61850.chapter17.l17.p02: Observe application behavior as well as link status. A successful cable-pull test can hide missing redundancy alarms, duplicate events or failed restoration. Test each independent path and confirm the normal configuration is recovered afterward.
iec61850.chapter17.l17.wf01: Predict surviving paths for each failure
iec61850.chapter17.l17.wf02: Apply one controlled fault at a time
iec61850.chapter17.l17.wf03: Record application continuity, diagnostics and restoration
iec61850.chapter17.l17.example: Disconnect 33-F01's PRP LAN A path, verify acquisition through B and inspect the redundancy alarm. Restore A, then repeat for B without joining the two LANs.
iec61850.chapter17.l17.check: Do not generalize single-link results to shared power failure, endpoint failure or multiple simultaneous faults that were not covered.
iec61850.chapter17.l18.title: Practical 33 kV Feeder FAT Procedure
iec61850.chapter17.l18.p01: The feeder FAT procedure combines document review, input simulation, protection/communication checks and operator-interface validation for one representative 33 kV bay. It uses the exact configuration intended for delivery.
iec61850.chapter17.l18.p02: Prepare expected results before testing and isolate outputs. A complete sequence includes normal indication, a representative protection operation, reporting, GOOSE where assigned, control rejection and communication recovery. Protection setting verification follows its own approved procedure.
iec61850.chapter17.l18.wf01: Verify 33-F01 identity, settings and signal list
iec61850.chapter17.l18.wf02: Execute normal, fault-indication and control cases
iec61850.chapter17.l18.wf03: Test failure recovery, resolve punch points and archive the tested revision
iec61850.chapter17.l18.example: The evidence sheet links each stimulus to IED state, transmitted service, subscriber/HMI result and witness. Test equipment and simulated breaker status are recorded explicitly.
iec61850.chapter17.l18.check: Any correction to the tested configuration requires repeat tests for affected functions before closing the FAT record.
iec61850.chapter17.l19.title: Practical 132/33 kV SAT Procedure
iec61850.chapter17.l19.p01: The station SAT procedure confirms installed bays, networks, timing and station/remote interfaces against the accepted design. It must coordinate with site access, isolation and operational responsibilities.
iec61850.chapter17.l19.p02: Begin with identity and wiring checks, then perform functional tests in approved stages. Reconcile FAT punch points and site changes into as-built records. Avoid active network or control testing on live connected schemes without the approved boundary.
iec61850.chapter17.l19.wf01: Verify installed 132/33 kV equipment and documentation
iec61850.chapter17.l19.wf02: Test point paths, control boundaries and redundancy
iec61850.chapter17.l19.wf03: Restore normal state and obtain the required witnessed release
iec61850.chapter17.l19.example: The 33-F01 bay is checked against its actual terminal schedule and fibre ports, while the 132 kV process-bus interfaces receive their specific measurement/timing tests where installed.
iec61850.chapter17.l19.check: The SAT report must distinguish completed, deferred and excluded tests and state any operating restriction associated with an unresolved issue.
iec61850.chapter17.l20.title: Test Reports, Punch Points and Troubleshooting
iec61850.chapter17.l20.p01: Test reports preserve the requirement, stimulus, expected result, observed result and evidence for each case. Punch points record deviations with severity, owner, corrective action and retest status.
iec61850.chapter17.l20.p02: A pass should be reproducible from the documented configuration and method. Do not close an issue because a symptom disappeared after a reboot without identifying what changed. Link capture files, logs and drawings to the relevant test ID.
iec61850.chapter17.l20.wf03: Repeat affected tests and issue the controlled final report
iec61850.chapter17.l20.example: A 33-F01 wrong-scale finding includes the injected current, displayed value, mapping correction and successful retest at several points. The final database revision is attached.
iec61850.chapter17.l20.check: Separate measured results from engineering analysis and remaining assumptions; never mark an unexecuted test as passed.
iec61850.chapter18.l01.title: Introduction to Wireshark
iec61850.chapter18.l01.p01: Wireshark decodes captured network traffic so engineers can inspect addresses, protocol exchanges and timing observations. It is an observation tool, not proof that a protection application or physical output behaved correctly.
iec61850.chapter18.l01.p02: The capture point determines what can be seen. A laptop connected to an ordinary switch port may receive broadcasts and selected multicast but not another device's unicast MMS conversation. Use approved mirror or TAP arrangements and preserve original captures.
iec61850.chapter18.l01.wf02: Choose a capture point that sees the relevant path
iec61850.chapter18.l01.wf03: Decode and correlate traffic with endpoint logs
iec61850.chapter18.l01.example: For 33-F01 reporting, capture the gateway-to-IED path and inject one known isolated status transition. Compare the report with the HMI event.
iec61850.chapter18.l01.check: Label synthetic field examples as illustrative; never present a constructed packet worksheet as a measured station capture.
iec61850.chapter18.l02.title: Packet Capture Fundamentals
iec61850.chapter18.l02.p01: Packet capture requires suitable interfaces, placement and storage. Port mirroring copies selected traffic, while a TAP provides an observation path according to its design. Both can have limitations that affect conclusions.
iec61850.chapter18.l02.p02: Check capture drops, link capacity, timestamp method and VLAN offload behavior. A saturated mirror port can omit packets even when the operational network delivers them correctly. Capture filters discard traffic at collection time; display filters only change what is shown afterward.
iec61850.chapter18.l02.wf02: Capture enough context before and after the event
iec61850.chapter18.l02.wf03: Record interface statistics and preserve the unfiltered file
iec61850.chapter18.l02.example: The 33-F01 exercise records association startup and a breaker transition, avoiding an overly narrow filter that would hide connection negotiation or a competing publisher.
iec61850.chapter18.l02.check: Do not connect an active test publisher to the station merely to obtain traffic; passive observation and active injection are different activities.
iec61850.chapter18.l03.title: Ethernet Frame Analysis
iec61850.chapter18.l03.p01: Ethernet analysis begins with source/destination MAC addresses, tagging and EtherType. These fields show how a frame should be delivered and which upper-layer decoder is relevant.
iec61850.chapter18.l03.p02: GOOSE and SV use their own Ethernet mappings, while MMS normally appears inside IP/TCP. A VLAN tag absent from a capture may have been removed by NIC offload or mirror behavior. Validate capture visibility before concluding that the sender is untagged.
iec61850.chapter18.l03.wf02: Check VLAN ID and priority where visible
iec61850.chapter18.l03.wf03: Compare the observed path with the switch configuration
iec61850.chapter18.l03.example: GOOSE EtherType 0x88B8 and SV EtherType 0x88BA distinguish the two conventional Layer-2 services. The station's IP traffic uses its appropriate IP EtherType instead.
iec61850.chapter18.l03.check: Do not interpret every multicast destination as GOOSE; identify the actual service and payload.
iec61850.chapter18.l04.title: IP and TCP Analysis
iec61850.chapter18.l04.p01: IP analysis checks endpoint addresses, subnet/routing assumptions and packet delivery. TCP analysis adds connection setup, sequencing, acknowledgments, retransmission and stream behavior for connection-oriented services such as the conventional MMS mapping.
iec61850.chapter18.l04.p02: TCP retransmissions can result from loss or delayed acknowledgments, while apparent errors may come from incomplete capture. Reassemble the stream before judging higher-layer data. One TCP segment is not necessarily one MMS message.
iec61850.chapter18.l04.wf03: Follow the reassembled stream and compare application responses
iec61850.chapter18.l04.example: For 33-F01, filter ip.addr == 192.168.100.31 and inspect the connection to Gateway A. A rejected application association is distinguished from an unanswered TCP SYN.
iec61850.chapter18.l04.check: Record capture completeness and endpoint logs before attributing every retransmission to a faulty switch.
iec61850.chapter18.l05.title: MMS Packet Identification
iec61850.chapter18.l05.p01: MMS identification starts with the conventional TCP 102 path and the decoded protocol. The mms display filter selects decoded MMS content, while tcp.port == 102 also shows transport and related setup traffic.
iec61850.chapter18.l05.p02: If MMS does not decode, check whether the capture includes the necessary stream data and whether reassembly is enabled. A nonstandard or security-enabled configuration requires its documented analysis method rather than forcing an incorrect decoder.
iec61850.chapter18.l05.wf03: Expand decoded MMS services and identify their purpose
iec61850.chapter18.l05.example: The 33-F01 gateway stream contains reads and reports after association. The engineer labels each operation rather than treating all TCP 102 payloads as identical measurement updates.
iec61850.chapter18.l05.check: An open TCP 102 connection proves transport establishment only, not successful reporting or control.
iec61850.chapter18.l06.title: MMS Association Analysis
iec61850.chapter18.l06.p01: Association analysis finds the stage at which the client-server relationship succeeds or fails. The conventional sequence includes TCP setup, COTP connection and application association/MMS initiation.
iec61850.chapter18.l06.p02: A rejection carries different meaning from silence or a reset. Compare selectors, application context, access policy and resource availability according to the actual device implementation. Preserve the first failed response instead of repeatedly restarting both endpoints.
iec61850.chapter18.l06.wf03: Compare the rejection or missing response with client and server diagnostics
iec61850.chapter18.l06.example: Gateway A reaches 33-F01's TCP listener but receives an association rejection. Investigation focuses on application parameters and policy rather than changing an already working VLAN path.
iec61850.chapter18.l06.check: Do not infer exact rejection semantics from a generic HMI 'offline' label; inspect the decoded response and device log.
iec61850.chapter18.l07.title: MMS Read and Reporting Analysis
iec61850.chapter18.l07.p01: Read analysis links a confirmed request to its response and verifies the returned type and value. Reporting analysis examines unsolicited information reports, selected members and relevant optional fields.
iec61850.chapter18.l07.p02: The decoded payload must be interpreted against the configured DataSet and model. An inclusion bitstring means an event report may omit unchanged members. Source event time, report time and capture time serve different purposes and should not be merged.
iec61850.chapter18.l07.wf01: Identify the requested reference or report identity
iec61850.chapter18.l07.wf02: Compare types, inclusion and values with the configuration
iec61850.chapter18.l07.wf03: Trace the result into the gateway tag and HMI
iec61850.chapter18.l07.example: After an isolated 33-F01 position change, inspect the actual included members and quality/time structures. A scalar stVal update does not imply separate q and t members were retransmitted.
iec61850.chapter18.l07.check: If packets are correct but the display is wrong, move the investigation to mapping and client processing.
iec61850.chapter18.l08.title: GOOSE Packet Identification
iec61850.chapter18.l08.p01: GOOSE identification uses EtherType and the goose decoder, followed by stream identity and payload inspection. Conventional GOOSE is Layer-2 multicast and has no TCP session to follow.
iec61850.chapter18.l08.p02: Several streams may share a capture point. Filter by the approved APPID or destination MAC, then verify the control-block reference, DataSet and configuration revision. A matching address alone is insufficient to prove the right application stream.
iec61850.chapter18.l08.wf03: Compare identity and data types with the approved SCD
iec61850.chapter18.l08.example: For 33-F01, goose.appid == 0x1001 selects the illustrative allocation. The engineer still checks gocbRef and ordered members before interpreting the trip Boolean.
iec61850.chapter18.l08.check: Remember that routed GOOSE is a different architecture; this lesson's Ethernet fields describe conventional station-LAN GOOSE.
iec61850.chapter18.l09.title: GOOSE APPID and VLAN Analysis
iec61850.chapter18.l09.p01: APPID and VLAN analysis compares the transmitted stream with the engineering allocation and switch path. Numeric bases must be explicit because SCL and tools can display the same value differently.
iec61850.chapter18.l09.p02: VLAN 200 decimal corresponds to hexadecimal 0C8, while an APPID displayed as 1001 hex equals a different decimal value. Misreading the base can produce a valid-looking but wrong configuration. Also verify PCP separately from VLAN membership.
iec61850.chapter18.l09.wf01: Record each field with its numeric base
iec61850.chapter18.l09.wf02: Compare publisher export and live frame
iec61850.chapter18.l09.wf03: Inspect every intermediate port's VLAN treatment
iec61850.chapter18.l09.example: The 33-F01 stream uses APPID 0x1001 and VLAN 200. If the receiver expects decimal 1001 as the APPID, the mismatch is corrected through the coordinated configuration.
iec61850.chapter18.l09.check: If a tag is missing in capture, verify offload/mirror behavior before editing the publisher.
iec61850.chapter18.l10.title: GOOSE stNum and sqNum Analysis
iec61850.chapter18.l10.p01: stNum and sqNum help distinguish GOOSE state changes from retransmission of the same state. Inspect them alongside payload, timestamp and configuration revision rather than using a counter alone as an event record.
iec61850.chapter18.l10.p02: Restarts, wraparound and redundancy duplicates complicate interpretation. Two copies seen on a PRP observation path can share application counters without representing two physical events. The subscriber should process the intended state according to its supported behavior.
iec61850.chapter18.l10.wf03: Compare counters and payload across the first event frame and later repeats
iec61850.chapter18.l10.example: An illustrative sequence changes from 17/6 to 18/0, followed by 18/1 and 18/2. The unchanged trip payload in the latter frames is expected retransmission.
iec61850.chapter18.l10.check: Do not count every GOOSE packet as another trip operation or alarm occurrence.
iec61850.chapter18.l11.title: GOOSE Retransmission Analysis
iec61850.chapter18.l11.p01: GOOSE timing analysis examines the rapid post-change retransmissions and the later steady heartbeat. The exact schedule belongs to the implementation and configuration, so measured intervals should be compared with the approved expectations.
iec61850.chapter18.l11.p02: timeAllowedtoLive supports receiver supervision of freshness. It is not a direct measurement of complete protection transfer time. Capture timestamps also include the observation method's uncertainty and may not represent the exact wire departure time.
iec61850.chapter18.l11.wf01: Measure intervals within one identified stream
iec61850.chapter18.l11.wf03: Test subscriber expiry under controlled stream loss
iec61850.chapter18.l11.example: The 33-F01 capture shows a burst after the trip member changes and increasing spacing afterward. The receiver's timeout alarm is checked separately from the packet timeline.
iec61850.chapter18.l11.check: Use suitable synchronized measurement equipment when the acceptance requirement concerns end-to-end protection timing.
iec61850.chapter18.l12.title: Sampled Values Packet Analysis
iec61850.chapter18.l12.p01: SV analysis checks stream identity, ASDU structure, sample counters, rate and quality according to the selected profile. Use the sv decoder and inspect fields supported by the installed Wireshark version.
iec61850.chapter18.l12.p02: Sample rate and frame rate differ when several ASDUs are packed into one frame. Counter gaps can arise from capture loss, so compare receiver statistics and mirror-port capacity. Correct packet structure does not prove correct analogue scaling or phase mapping.
iec61850.chapter18.l12.wf01: Filter the assigned APPID or svID
iec61850.chapter18.l12.wf02: Inspect all ASDUs and counter progression
iec61850.chapter18.l12.wf03: Correlate anomalies with receiver health and waveform injection results
iec61850.chapter18.l12.example: For MU_132_L01, record sv.smpCnt progression and the agreed frame packing. A phase-current test verifies the semantic channel mapping beyond the packet decoder.
iec61850.chapter18.l12.check: Do not infer primary amperes directly from an encoded sample integer without the profile's scaling and channel definition.
iec61850.chapter18.l13.title: PTP and SNTP Packet Analysis
iec61850.chapter18.l13.p01: Timing-packet analysis verifies that expected PTP or NTP/SNTP exchanges reach the endpoint. PTP inspection includes profile-relevant message types, domain and source identity; SNTP uses its configured IP service path.
iec61850.chapter18.l13.p02: Packet visibility cannot establish endpoint clock accuracy by itself. Wrong profile, asymmetry or clock handling can produce poor synchronization with apparently normal traffic. Correlate packet observations with clock offset, quality and application measurements.
iec61850.chapter18.l13.wf02: Inspect source identity and expected exchanges
iec61850.chapter18.l13.wf03: Compare endpoint status and measured timing against requirements
iec61850.chapter18.l13.example: The station exercise uses ptp or ntp display filters as appropriate. MU_132_L01's PTP health is compared with its sample synchronization indication during a reference interruption.
iec61850.chapter18.l13.check: Keep protocol decoding and accuracy measurement as separate tests; one cannot substitute for the other.
iec61850.chapter18.l14.title: VLAN and Multicast Troubleshooting
iec61850.chapter18.l14.p01: VLAN and multicast troubleshooting locates where a required stream is filtered, flooded or misclassified. Compare the publisher port, trunks and subscriber port using both configuration and observed traffic.
iec61850.chapter18.l14.p02: Ordinary IP multicast snooping does not automatically manage conventional GOOSE/SV groups. Static or other supported industrial filtering must match the intended subscriptions. A mirror configuration can also hide traffic, so verify the observation path.
iec61850.chapter18.l14.wf01: Confirm source frame identity and tag
iec61850.chapter18.l14.wf03: Capture near the subscriber and compare with its receive diagnostic
iec61850.chapter18.l14.example: If VLAN 200 GOOSE leaves 33-F01 but an uplink admits only VLAN 100, the path fails while MMS remains available. The corrected rule is then tested at every required subscriber.
iec61850.chapter18.l14.check: Avoid permanently enabling unrestricted flooding as a workaround without reviewing network capacity and the original policy.
iec61850.chapter18.l15.title: TCP Connection Troubleshooting
iec61850.chapter18.l15.p01: TCP connection troubleshooting separates reachability, listener availability, handshake completion and application setup. SYN retries, resets and established streams suggest different next checks but require context.
iec61850.chapter18.l15.p02: A reset can come from an endpoint or another network device; silence can reflect filtering, routing or an unavailable server. Compare both directions and use endpoint logs. Once transport succeeds, investigate association and service behavior separately.
iec61850.chapter18.l15.wf03: Correlate with server availability and network policy
iec61850.chapter18.l15.example: Gateway A's SYN to 33-F01 receives no reply. Check address ownership, route and permitted TCP 102 path before editing report triggers that have not yet been reached.
iec61850.chapter18.l15.check: Do not diagnose an application-specific access failure from TCP flags alone; inspect the higher-layer response when available.
iec61850.chapter18.l16.title: IED-to-SCADA Communication Failure
iec61850.chapter18.l16.p01: An IED-to-SCADA failure can occur at the source model, network, association, acquisition resource or point database. The same offline icon can hide several distinct causes.
iec61850.chapter18.l16.p02: Use a controlled read or known source transition to locate the last correct boundary. If reads succeed but reports do not, inspect RCB allocation and triggers. If reports decode correctly but the display is wrong, inspect mapping and quality policy.
iec61850.chapter18.l16.wf03: Trace the acquired value through driver, tag and display
iec61850.chapter18.l16.example: For 33-F01, a correctly decoded breaker report reaches Gateway A but the HMI remains unchanged. The investigation checks the bound tag and state conversion before changing network settings.
iec61850.chapter18.l16.check: Save the failing capture and configuration revision so the corrective action can be verified against the original symptom.
iec61850.chapter18.l17.title: GOOSE Subscription Failure
iec61850.chapter18.l17.p01: GOOSE subscription failure may reflect absent publication, wrong delivery, configuration mismatch or unbound application input. A receiving NIC can see traffic that the IEC 61850 application correctly rejects.
iec61850.chapter18.l17.p02: Compare APPID, MAC, VLAN, control-block identity, ConfRev and ordered data types, then inspect internal binding. Test and simulation indications may also influence acceptance according to the device's supported mode. Avoid disabling supervision just to make the alarm disappear.
iec61850.chapter18.l17.wf02: Compare traffic at the receiver with its configuration
iec61850.chapter18.l17.wf03: Inspect acceptance diagnostics and internal logic transition
iec61850.chapter18.l17.example: 33-F01's new DataSet revision reaches the receiving IED, but the old subscriber configuration rejects it. Update the coordinated engineering files and retest rather than forcing acceptance of an unknown layout.
iec61850.chapter18.l17.check: After repair, repeat timeout and invalid-data tests as well as the successful signal transition.
iec61850.chapter18.l18.title: Practical Packet Capture — 33 kV Feeder
iec61850.chapter18.l18.p01: The practical capture exercise observes one 33 kV feeder in a controlled test arrangement. It records MMS association, a known breaker-state event and the assigned GOOSE transition where configured.
iec61850.chapter18.l18.p02: Begin before the event and retain context afterward. Record stimulus time, test mode, device revisions and capture placement. The illustrative field worksheet is a guide to inspection; actual acceptance evidence comes from the saved measured capture and endpoint observations.
iec61850.chapter18.l18.wf01: Set the approved mirror/TAP and start capture
iec61850.chapter18.l18.wf03: Save pcapng and correlate MMS, GOOSE and HMI results
iec61850.chapter18.l18.example: The worksheet expects the assigned IP endpoint, APPID 0x1001 and VLAN 200. A stable GOOSE repeat is distinguished from the first state-change frame and from an MMS report.
iec61850.chapter18.l18.check: Record dropped-packet statistics and avoid claiming a missing frame proves operational network loss without corroboration.
iec61850.chapter18.l19.title: Advanced IEC 61850 Troubleshooting Workflow
iec61850.chapter18.l19.p01: Advanced troubleshooting uses hypotheses and boundary evidence rather than random configuration changes. Define the symptom, expected behavior, last known good revision and a test that can distinguish competing causes.
iec61850.chapter18.l19.p02: Work from the simplest failed layer toward the application, while preserving evidence. Compare a working path or device only when its relevant settings and role are understood. A difference is a clue, not automatically the root cause.
iec61850.chapter18.l19.wf02: Collect source, network and destination evidence
iec61850.chapter18.l19.wf03: Change one cause, repeat the test and document the conclusion
iec61850.chapter18.l19.example: For intermittent 33-F01 reporting, correlate TCP recovery, RCB state and gateway logs with switch counters. A coincident packet gap at an overloaded mirror is not enough to blame the station link.
iec61850.chapter18.l19.check: End with a reproducible cause-and-effect result and the tested final revision, including any remaining uncertainty.
iec61850.chapter18.l20.title: Wireshark Interview and Practical Questions
iec61850.chapter18.l20.p01: Practical interview questions should test reasoning from evidence. Ask why ping can succeed while GOOSE fails, why TCP 102 can connect while MMS association fails, and why correct packets can coexist with an incorrect HMI indication.
iec61850.chapter18.l20.p02: Good answers distinguish protocol layers and application semantics: ping tests an IP path, association adds application negotiation, and mapping still governs presentation. Counter and timestamp questions should consider retransmission, capture placement and source-time quality rather than memorize one screenshot.
iec61850.chapter18.l20.wf01: Explain the hypothesis for each symptom
iec61850.chapter18.l20.wf02: Name the next observation that would distinguish causes
iec61850.chapter18.l20.wf03: State what the evidence cannot prove
iec61850.chapter18.l20.example: Exercise: stNum stays 18 while sqNum increases and payload stays true. Answer: this is consistent with repeated transmission of one GOOSE state, not proof of repeated physical trips. Confirm identity and restart context.
iec61850.chapter18.l20.check: Exercise: an SV counter gap appears only in a saturated mirror capture. Check capture drops and subscriber statistics before concluding the protection IED lost samples.
iec61850.chapter19.l01.title: Introduction to Multi-Vendor IEC 61850 Systems
iec61850.chapter19.l01.p01: Multi-vendor IEC 61850 systems combine devices and tools from different suppliers within one engineered application. Standardized models and services provide a foundation, but supported options, firmware and application bindings still require verification.
iec61850.chapter19.l01.p02: Integration succeeds when both transport and meaning agree. A Boolean received successfully can still represent the wrong protection stage, while two similarly named objects can expose different optional attributes. Use a controlled compatibility and signal matrix.
iec61850.chapter19.l01.wf03: Test representative combinations before station-wide rollout
iec61850.chapter19.l01.example: The 33 kV pilot combines a feeder publisher, another supplier's controller and a gateway client. Each exchange has a documented source, type, destination and failure response.
iec61850.chapter19.l01.check: Avoid claiming universal interoperability from vendor logos or an IEC 61850 checkbox; verify the delivered combination.
iec61850.chapter19.l02.title: Interoperability and Conformance
iec61850.chapter19.l02.p01: Conformance testing assesses implementation behavior against specified standard tests. Interoperability testing checks whether implementations work together, while project acceptance checks the actual engineered application against requirements.
iec61850.chapter19.l02.p02: A conformance certificate has a scope, version and tested capability set. It does not certify every future firmware or custom station configuration. Read the certificate together with PICS, MICS, PIXIT and other applicable implementation statements.
iec61850.chapter19.l02.wf01: Verify certificate scope and firmware relevance
iec61850.chapter19.l02.wf02: Compare claimed services with project needs
iec61850.chapter19.l02.wf03: Run joint functional and negative tests
iec61850.chapter19.l02.example: Two certified IEDs can still fail a GOOSE exchange because the configured member types or receiving application binding differ. The integration test resolves that specific combination.
iec61850.chapter19.l02.check: Keep compliance evidence and project test results linked but distinct; neither should be presented as a substitute for the other.
iec61850.chapter19.l03.title: Siemens SIPROTEC IED Integration
iec61850.chapter19.l03.p01: Siemens SIPROTEC integration begins with the exact product generation, hardware and firmware. DIGSI 5 serves SIPROTEC 5 engineering, while other generations can use different tools; the IEC 61850 System Configurator supports the system exchange workflow.
iec61850.chapter19.l03.p02: Do not infer optional service or process-bus capability from the family name. Collect the device's actual model and supported engineering packages, then review how system configuration and internal application settings are exchanged and retained.
iec61850.chapter19.l03.wf01: Identify the SIPROTEC variant and approved tool versions
iec61850.chapter19.l03.wf03: Integrate and verify reports, subscriptions and controls
iec61850.chapter19.l03.example: In the pilot, a SIPROTEC-family feeder IED publishes a supported operation signal. The test verifies its actual reference and received type rather than assuming every SIPROTEC exposes the same LN instance.
iec61850.chapter19.l03.check: Archive both device and system engineering projects needed to reproduce the tested configuration; menu names depend on the installed versions.
iec61850.chapter19.l04.title: Schneider MiCOM IED Integration
iec61850.chapter19.l04.p01: Schneider MiCOM integration requires identifying the exact device lineage, model and firmware. Schneider documents Easergy Studio as the successor name to MiCOM S1 Studio; compatible data-model packages and device support must be checked for the selected relay.
iec61850.chapter19.l04.p02: The MiCOM name spans product histories, so do not assume every MiCOM device uses the same tool or capabilities. Configuration exchange, optional services and internal input mapping remain model-specific. Preserve the original project before tool conversion.
iec61850.chapter19.l04.wf02: Obtain the matching data model and SCL export
iec61850.chapter19.l04.wf03: Test system exchange and application bindings
iec61850.chapter19.l04.example: The pilot's Schneider-family device acts as a designated subscriber only after its supported GOOSE features and input types are verified. No proprietary menu path is invented by this course.
iec61850.chapter19.l04.check: Check official support for the installed variant; another supplier's MiCOM-branded tool description is not automatic evidence of compatibility.
iec61850.chapter19.l05.title: ABB Relion IED Integration
iec61850.chapter19.l05.p01: ABB/Relion-family integration starts from the exact installed product and its supported engineering package. PCM600 and matching connectivity packages are used for supported Relion devices; product ownership and support channels vary across the installed portfolio.
iec61850.chapter19.l05.p02: A common family name does not imply identical hardware, object models or SCL workflows. Verify the relevant vendor documentation for the specific relay and firmware. System engineering and device application binding must be checked together after import.
iec61850.chapter19.l05.wf03: Integrate the exported model and verify internal signals
iec61850.chapter19.l05.example: The pilot's Relion-family controller receives the agreed feeder state and exposes its own status to the gateway. Both subscription diagnostics and application logic are observed during testing.
iec61850.chapter19.l05.check: Do not assume a connectivity package for one series can safely configure another series or firmware revision.
iec61850.chapter19.l06.title: GE Multilin IED Integration
iec61850.chapter19.l06.p01: GE Multilin integration depends on the selected relay family and firmware. For supported UR-family devices, EnerVista UR Setup provides relevant configuration functions, but other Multilin families can use different packages and workflows.
iec61850.chapter19.l06.p02: Review the actual IEC 61850 model, service limits and engineering exchange behavior. Firmware changes can affect supported functions or mappings, so a previously working template must be revalidated rather than copied blindly.
iec61850.chapter19.l06.wf01: Identify the exact Multilin family and tool package
iec61850.chapter19.l06.wf02: Export and review supported model information
iec61850.chapter19.l06.wf03: Test MMS, GOOSE and control behavior required by the project
iec61850.chapter19.l06.example: The pilot includes a Multilin-family IED as a station MMS server. The gateway maps its actual measurements and status objects instead of imposing another supplier's naming convention.
iec61850.chapter19.l06.check: Do not extrapolate a capability documented for one UR release to every GE relay; retain model-specific evidence.
iec61850.chapter19.l07.title: Vendor Engineering Tools Overview
iec61850.chapter19.l07.p01: Vendor tools configure device-specific applications, while system configurators coordinate shared SCL engineering. Both roles are needed when protection logic, hardware and communication relationships must remain consistent.
iec61850.chapter19.l07.p02: Tool compatibility includes software version, device package, firmware and supported SCL edition. Automatic conversion or import can change or discard information. A repeatable workflow records each exchange and validates the resulting online behavior.
iec61850.chapter19.l07.wf03: Preserve original and converted projects with comparison results
iec61850.chapter19.l07.example: The multi-vendor pilot uses each supplier's supported device tool and one controlled system-engineering process. The SCD owner coordinates exchanges rather than allowing independent conflicting station masters.
iec61850.chapter19.l07.check: Avoid publishing a universal click-by-click menu sequence for all vendors; use the exact product manual for implementation details.
iec61850.chapter19.l08.title: ICD File Collection and Validation
iec61850.chapter19.l08.p01: ICD collection establishes the capability inputs for system engineering. Files should come from trusted project/vendor sources and match the intended hardware, firmware and application options.
iec61850.chapter19.l08.p02: Validate syntax, schema compatibility and required model content before import. A generic library ICD may omit configured functions or describe features unavailable on the installed device. Keep provenance and checksum information so later changes can be traced.
iec61850.chapter19.l08.wf01: Collect the approved file and implementation statements
iec61850.chapter19.l08.wf03: Import into a pilot system and compare with the live device
iec61850.chapter19.l08.example: For the 33 kV pilot, every feeder and controller file is checked for the actual report and GOOSE requirements before address allocation and signal binding.
iec61850.chapter19.l08.check: Reject silent substitution of a similar model's ICD; a matching product-family name does not prove model equivalence.
iec61850.chapter19.l09.title: Multi-Vendor SCD Engineering
iec61850.chapter19.l09.p01: Multi-vendor SCD engineering coordinates device names, model instances, communication addresses and signal exchanges. The system configurator must preserve supported vendor information while maintaining consistent standardized references.
iec61850.chapter19.l09.p02: Define who owns each change and how device updates return to the system baseline. Concurrent unreviewed edits can create incompatible publisher/subscriber revisions even when each individual file imports successfully.
iec61850.chapter19.l09.wf02: Allocate names, reports and multicast streams
iec61850.chapter19.l09.wf03: Resolve dependencies and distribute controlled device outputs
iec61850.chapter19.l09.example: The pilot SCD records 33-F01's gcbTrip and every subscribing input. A member-order change is reviewed across all consumers before any device is downloaded.
iec61850.chapter19.l09.check: Keep the final as-built SCD aligned with deployed vendor projects and gateway databases, not merely the last file exported by one tool.
iec61850.chapter19.l10.title: Logical Node and Data Model Compatibility
iec61850.chapter19.l10.p01: Data-model compatibility concerns names, common data classes, attributes, functional constraints and supported semantic meaning. Different vendors may use prefixes, instances or logical-device organization differently while representing comparable functions.
iec61850.chapter19.l10.p02: Do not normalize by renaming until references merely look alike. Build a mapping that preserves the actual source and explains equivalence. Optional attributes and extensions must be handled explicitly rather than assumed present everywhere.
iec61850.chapter19.l10.wf01: Browse and compare relevant model structures
iec61850.chapter19.l10.wf02: Match engineering meaning and supported types
iec61850.chapter19.l10.wf03: Verify each mapped value with a known stimulus
iec61850.chapter19.l10.example: Two feeder relays expose phase current through their supported MMXU structures but use different logical-device names. The gateway maps each exact reference to a common engineering unit.
iec61850.chapter19.l10.check: Similar display labels are not sufficient; verify data type, quality association and whether the value is primary or secondary scaled.
iec61850.chapter19.l11.title: DataSet and Report Compatibility
iec61850.chapter19.l11.p01: Report compatibility includes DataSet structure, RCB features, trigger support and client interpretation. Differences in limits, reservation behavior or optional fields can affect redundant gateways and recovery.
iec61850.chapter19.l11.p02: Use the exact supported combination rather than enabling every optional field by habit. Test inclusion and timestamps for each DataSet structure, especially object-level selections versus separate scalar members. Buffered retention and restart behavior remain implementation-dependent.
iec61850.chapter19.l11.wf03: Test events, GI, integrity, ownership and reconnect
iec61850.chapter19.l11.example: Gateway A receives status reports from several vendors. The point database retains each DataSet's actual order and type structure rather than assuming all reports use the same template.
iec61850.chapter19.l11.check: Record unsupported recovery behavior and event-gap handling; a generic BRCB label does not guarantee identical retention across devices.
iec61850.chapter19.l12.title: Multi-Vendor GOOSE Engineering
iec61850.chapter19.l12.p01: Multi-vendor GOOSE requires agreement on stream identity, ordered payload types and application behavior. Network delivery is only the first stage; quality, test/simulation handling and timeout policy must also be compatible.
iec61850.chapter19.l12.p02: Run a pilot exchange using the exact delivered firmware and tool versions. Some optional data structures may require a different supported member selection. Any conversion must be documented and tested rather than guessed from encoded bytes.
iec61850.chapter19.l12.wf01: Compare publisher and subscriber capability statements
iec61850.chapter19.l12.wf02: Engineer a compatible DataSet and binding
iec61850.chapter19.l12.wf03: Test state changes, invalid data and stream loss
iec61850.chapter19.l12.example: The feeder publisher sends an agreed operation Boolean and supported quality information to the controller. The controller proves both internal input acceptance and the intended isolated output response.
iec61850.chapter19.l12.check: Do not disable quality or revision checks simply to make dissimilar configurations communicate.
iec61850.chapter19.l13.title: GOOSE Subscription Mapping
iec61850.chapter19.l13.p01: Subscription mapping translates external standardized references into the receiver's internal application inputs. The SCL exchange may identify the source correctly while a vendor-specific binding still needs completion.
iec61850.chapter19.l13.p02: Review member order, type conversion and source identity after every import. An internal input with a familiar name can remain connected to an old stream. Use online application diagnostics and known test transitions to prove the binding.
iec61850.chapter19.l13.wf01: Resolve the external reference and control-block context
iec61850.chapter19.l13.wf03: Test positive transition, invalid quality and expiry
iec61850.chapter19.l13.example: The pilot controller maps 33-F01's trip member to its designated input. A separate communication-health signal drives the approved supervision behavior rather than treating missing data as a valid false.
iec61850.chapter19.l13.check: Preserve the mapping report and vendor project; the SCD alone may not show every internal logic association.
iec61850.chapter19.l14.title: MMS Client Integration
iec61850.chapter19.l14.p01: MMS client integration across vendors requires model discovery, association compatibility, report allocation and data interpretation for each server. A single gateway driver can still need device-specific configuration.
iec61850.chapter19.l14.p02: Test client resource use under the intended number of simultaneous IEDs and redundant clients. A maintenance connection can expose limits hidden in a single-device demonstration. Quality, timestamps and control results must remain consistent at the engineering-tag layer.
iec61850.chapter19.l14.wf01: Create per-device connection and model records
iec61850.chapter19.l14.wf02: Allocate supported reports and access rights
iec61850.chapter19.l14.wf03: Test combined load, reconnect and control restrictions
iec61850.chapter19.l14.example: Gateway A reads the pilot's Siemens-, Schneider-, Relion- and Multilin-family devices through their actual supported references. Operator tags use common naming without changing source semantics.
iec61850.chapter19.l14.check: Do not assume the gateway's import success means every optional service or control model is supported.
iec61850.chapter19.l15.title: Time Synchronization Compatibility
iec61850.chapter19.l15.p01: Time compatibility requires more than devices advertising SNTP or PTP. Check implemented versions, profiles, domain behavior, timestamp quality and the accuracy required by each application.
iec61850.chapter19.l15.p02: Mixed-vendor timing chains can fail because of incompatible delay mechanisms or clock roles. Event displays can also differ because of local time-zone formatting even when source time is correct. Test source loss and recovery across the full system.
iec61850.chapter19.l15.wf03: Measure endpoint behavior and compare source timestamps through SCADA
iec61850.chapter19.l15.example: The pilot's monitoring IEDs use an approved station-time method, while any process-bus equipment uses its specifically supported precision profile. Their acceptance criteria remain distinct.
iec61850.chapter19.l15.check: Do not claim a common GNSS source automatically makes every endpoint synchronized to the required accuracy.
iec61850.chapter19.l16.title: Network and VLAN Compatibility
iec61850.chapter19.l16.p01: Network compatibility covers physical interfaces, tagging, multicast, redundancy and management behavior. Devices may interpret port roles or VLAN settings differently through their engineering tools.
iec61850.chapter19.l16.p02: Verify numerical values and live frames, especially where one tool displays hexadecimal and another decimal. PRP/HSR support must match the actual interface mode. Two physical ports do not establish a compatible redundancy implementation.
iec61850.chapter19.l16.wf03: Test normal and redundant paths at the application level
iec61850.chapter19.l16.example: The pilot's GOOSE stream uses VLAN 200 and APPID 0x1001 consistently. Each vendor's exported configuration and the switch path are checked against those numerical allocations.
iec61850.chapter19.l16.check: Avoid bridging PRP LANs to accommodate a single-attached device; use the approved connection arrangement or supported RedBox.
iec61850.chapter19.l17.title: Gateway and SCADA Integration
iec61850.chapter19.l17.p01: Gateway and SCADA integration provides a consistent operator view over different source models. Consistency should come from explicit mapping, not from discarding source quality or forcing all data into one simplistic type.
iec61850.chapter19.l17.p02: Normalize units and tag names while retaining traceability to original references. Controls, alarms and timestamps need per-source verification. Protocol conversion to the remote master must preserve agreed semantics and document unavoidable limitations.
iec61850.chapter19.l17.wf03: Test every source through HMI and remote destinations
iec61850.chapter19.l17.example: All pilot feeders display current in primary amperes, but the gateway conversion differs where source scaling differs. Double-point breaker states remain distinguishable from Boolean alarms.
iec61850.chapter19.l17.check: Test abnormal states and communication loss for every vendor; normal values alone do not reveal incompatible quality handling.
iec61850.chapter19.l18.title: Practical Multi-Vendor 33 kV Feeder Example
iec61850.chapter19.l18.p01: The practical multi-vendor feeder pilot uses one source protection IED, one receiving controller and the station gateway. Vendor families illustrate roles; the actual selected models and firmware determine supported functions.
iec61850.chapter19.l18.p02: Start with one complete function before expanding the station. The pilot includes model exchange, GOOSE binding, MMS reports, timing and operator presentation. Each interface has a positive test and at least one relevant failure test.
iec61850.chapter19.l18.wf03: Execute joint tests and publish the approved integration pattern
iec61850.chapter19.l18.example: Use the tutorial's 33-F01 address .31 and assigned GOOSE allocation consistently, while the receiving controller and gateway have their own identities. No device is assumed capable solely from its depicted appearance.
iec61850.chapter19.l18.check: Clone only the validated pattern; allocate new names, addresses and stream identities for every additional bay.
iec61850.chapter19.l19.title: Multi-Vendor FAT/SAT Testing
iec61850.chapter19.l19.p01: Multi-vendor FAT demonstrates the delivered combination under representative operation and failure conditions. SAT confirms installed paths, final firmware and as-built configurations still match that tested combination.
iec61850.chapter19.l19.p02: Include all responsible suppliers in issue resolution where needed. A failure should be described with source configuration, transmitted evidence and receiver behavior so ownership is based on facts rather than assumptions about another vendor.
iec61850.chapter19.l19.wf02: Record positive and negative results at both endpoints
iec61850.chapter19.l19.wf03: Resolve deviations and repeat affected joint tests
iec61850.chapter19.l19.example: The pilot test deliberately changes a source state, removes its stream and checks invalid quality. Gateway reports and control authority are tested alongside the inter-IED exchange.
iec61850.chapter19.l19.check: Do not close an interoperability issue from one supplier's isolated test alone when the failing behavior depends on the combined system.
iec61850.chapter19.l20.title: Interoperability Troubleshooting
iec61850.chapter19.l20.p01: Interoperability troubleshooting identifies where standards-compatible capabilities or configured semantics diverge. Compare edition, service support, types, stream identity, binding and failure behavior systematically.
iec61850.chapter19.l20.p02: Preserve exact files and traces from both ends. A protocol decoder can confirm transmitted content, while vendor diagnostics reveal why a receiver rejected or ignored it. Avoid undocumented type reinterpretation or disabled supervision as permanent fixes.
iec61850.chapter19.l20.wf02: Compare capability and live behavior at each boundary
iec61850.chapter19.l20.wf03: Implement a supported correction and repeat the joint test
iec61850.chapter19.l20.example: If 33-F01 publishes the correct Boolean but the controller expects a structured object at that member position, correct the coordinated DataSet/binding agreement rather than relabeling the packet.
iec61850.chapter19.l20.check: Archive the final compatibility decision, tested versions and known limitations for future firmware changes and device replacement.
iec61850.chapter20.l01.title: Project Introduction and Scope
iec61850.chapter20.l01.p01: This illustrative project engineers a 132/33/11 kV station from requirements through acceptance. The fixed scope is one 132 kV incoming line 132-L01, transformer T1 at 132/33 kV, two 33 kV bus sections, coupler 33-BC01, two 33 kV outgoing circuits, transformer T2 at 33/11 kV and two 11 kV feeders.
